title: Obesity in Children is Associated With Increased Dengue Virus Binding, but not Neutralizing, Antibody Responses Following Primary Infection
abstract: Abstract Background Obesity has been associated with higher risk of dengue virus (DENV) infection and disease, yet its influence on antibody responses to DENV remains undefined. Methods We evaluated whether nutritional status—based on body mass index z-score (BMIz)—or blood markers of body fat—leptin and adiponectin—are associated with binding and/or neutralizing antibody responses to DENV in 85 children in the Nicaraguan Pediatric Dengue Cohort Study who experienced a primary DENV infection in 2019. Associations were estimated using linear models adjusting for age, sex, and DENV infection outcome. Results Compared with children with normal weight, those with obesity had higher quantities of DENV binding antibodies (fold-change [FC] 1.89, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.02, 3.48) but no difference in neutralizing antibodies. Likewise, leptin concentration was associated with higher quantities of binding antibodies (FC 1.22, 95% CI 1.09, 1.37), while adiponectin was associated with lower quantities (FC 0.79, 95% CI .67, .94), and neither was associated with neutralizing antibodies. Lower neutralizing efficiency (neutralizing/binding antibodies) was observed in children with obesity (FC 0.67, 95% CI .48, .93). Conclusions Our results indicate that obesity is associated with higher antibody quantity (binding) but not higher quality (neutralization) postprimary DENV infection—implying that antibodies generated by children with obesity have lower neutralization efficiency, requiring greater quantities to reach similar levels of neutralization than children with normal weight. Further, the agreement among the 3 models using distinct proxies of body fat—BMIz, leptin, and adiponectin—demonstrates that adipokines are useful in supplementing BMIz analysis or as independent predictors of immune responses.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the association between obesity and antibody responses to dengue virus in children, addressing the gap in understanding how nutritional status influences immune responses to dengue infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated 85 children from the Nicaraguan Pediatric Dengue Cohort Study who experienced a primary dengue virus infection in 2019, assessing the impact of body mass index z-score, leptin, and adiponectin on binding and neutralizing antibody responses.
analysis.methods: Associations were estimated using linear models adjusting for age, sex, and dengue infection outcome, with binding and neutralizing antibody responses measured using specific assays.
analysis.main_results: Children with obesity had higher quantities of binding antibodies but no difference in neutralizing antibodies compared to those with normal weight. Leptin was associated with higher binding antibodies, while adiponectin was associated with lower binding antibodies, with no effect on neutralizing antibodies.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that obesity is associated with higher antibody quantity (binding) but not higher quality (neutralization) post-primary dengue infection, implying lower neutralization efficiency in children with obesity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results indicate that adipokines, such as leptin and adiponectin, are useful in supplementing BMIz analysis or as independent predictors of immune responses, highlighting the importance of considering body fat markers in understanding immune responses to dengue virus.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study design limitations include the observational nature and the potential for confounding factors, which may affect the strength of the evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the impact of obesity on antibody responses to dengue virus in children, finding that obesity was associated with higher binding antibodies but not neutralizing antibodies, suggesting lower neutralization efficiency in obese children.

elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated 85 children from the Nicaraguan Pediatric Dengue Cohort Study who experienced a primary dengue virus infection in 2019, assessing the impact of body mass index z-score, leptin, and adiponectin on binding and neutralizing antibody responses.
elements_en.methods: Associations were estimated using linear models adjusting for age, sex, and dengue infection outcome, with binding and neutralizing antibody responses measured using specific assays.
elements_en.main_results: Children with obesity had higher quantities of binding antibodies but no difference in neutralizing antibodies compared to those with normal weight. Leptin was associated with higher binding antibodies, while adiponectin was associated with lower binding antibodies, with no effect on neutralizing antibodies.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that obesity is associated with higher antibody quantity (binding) but not higher quality (neutralization) post-primary dengue infection, implying lower neutralization efficiency in children with obesity.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results indicate that adipokines, such as leptin and adiponectin, are useful in supplementing BMIz analysis or as independent predictors of immune responses, highlighting the importance of considering body fat markers in understanding immune responses to dengue virus.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study design limitations include the observational nature and the potential for confounding factors, which may affect the strength of the evidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨儿童肥胖与登革病毒(DENV)抗体反应之间的关联,填补了对营养状况如何影响登革病毒(DENV)感染的抗体反应理解的空白。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究评估了85名来自尼加拉瓜儿科登革热研究(Nicaraguan Pediatric Dengue 队列研究 Study)的儿童,这些儿童在2019年经历了初次登革病毒(DENV)感染,研究了体重指数z值、瘦素和脂联素对结合和中和抗体反应的影响。
elements_zh.methods: 通过线性模型调整年龄、性别和登革热感染结果来估计相关性,结合和中和抗体反应通过特定的实验方法进行测量。
elements_zh.main_results: 与体重正常的儿童相比,肥胖儿童的结合抗体数量更高,但中和抗体无差异。瘦素与更高的结合抗体数量相关,而脂联素与更低的结合抗体数量相关,两者均未影响中和抗体水平。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,肥胖与初次感染后DENV结合抗体数量增加有关,但与中和抗体质量无关,暗示肥胖儿童的抗体中和效率较低。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果表明,瘦素和脂联素等脂联素类物质可用于补充BMIz分析或作为独立的免疫应答预测因子,强调了在理解登革病毒(DENV)感染中考虑脂肪标志物的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 研究设计的局限性包括其观察性质以及可能存在的混杂因素,这可能影响证据的强度。

title_zh: 儿童肥胖与初次感染后登革病毒(DENV)结合抗体反应增加有关,但与中和抗体反应无关
source_body_en: Abstract Background Obesity has been associated with higher risk of dengue virus (DENV) infection and disease, yet its influence on antibody responses to DENV remains undefined. Methods We evaluated whether nutritional status—based on body mass index z-score (BMIz)—or blood markers of body fat—leptin and adiponectin—are associated with binding and/or neutralizing antibody responses to DENV in 85 children in the Nicaraguan Pediatric Dengue Cohort Study who experienced a primary DENV infection in 2019. Associations were estimated using linear models adjusting for age, sex, and DENV infection outcome. Results Compared with children with normal weight, those with obesity had higher quantities of DENV binding antibodies (fold-change [FC] 1.89, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.02, 3.48) but no difference in neutralizing antibodies. Likewise, leptin concentration was associated with higher quantities of binding antibodies (FC 1.22, 95% CI 1.09, 1.37), while adiponectin was associated with lower quantities (FC 0.79, 95% CI .67, .94), and neither was associated with neutralizing antibodies. Lower neutralizing efficiency (neutralizing/binding antibodies) was observed in children with obesity (FC 0.67, 95% CI .48, .93). Conclusions Our results indicate that obesity is associated with higher antibody quantity (binding) but not higher quality (neutralization) postprimary DENV infection—implying that antibodies generated by children with obesity have lower neutralization efficiency, requiring greater quantities to reach similar levels of neutralization than children with normal weight. Further, the agreement among the 3 models using distinct proxies of body fat—BMIz, leptin, and adiponectin—demonstrates that adipokines are useful in supplementing BMIz analysis or as independent predictors of immune responses.

title: Presence of Heterozygous V1016G kdr Mutation in Pyrethroid Insecticide Resistance in Aedes aegypti a Dengue vector from Southern India.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aedes aegypti is a primary vector of Dengue, Chikungunya, and Zika viruses, and its control relies heavily on pyrethroid insecticides. However, the development of resistance in mosquito populations poses a major challenge to effective vector control. This study aimed to investigate the presence of the V1016G knockdown resistance (kdr) mutation in Aedes aegypti collected from Nagapattinam district, Tamil Nadu, India. METHODS: Aedes immatures were collected from selected field sites and subjected to insecticide susceptibility testing using World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines. Genomic DNA was extracted, and allele-specific PCR was performed to detect the V1016G mutation in the voltage-gated sodium channel gene (vgsc). RESULTS: The analysis revealed the presence of the V1016G mutation in heterozygous form (VG) among the tested samples. No homozygous mutants (GG) were detected. The presence of heterozygous individuals indicates an early stage of resistance development, likely due to ongoing insecticide selection pressure. Bioassay results showed reduced susceptibility to pyrethroids in these populations, supporting the molecular findings. CONCLUSION: This study provides baseline data on the genetic mechanism of pyrethroid resistance in Aedes aegypti from Nagapattinam district. Regular monitoring of kdr mutations is essential to detect resistance early and guide insecticide use policies. title: Synergistic Effects of pH and Temperature on Dengue Virus Envelope Dimers: Insights from Microsecond Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
abstract: Dengue pathogenesis depends on a conformational rearrangement of the envelope glycoprotein (pE) induced by low pH. However, how pH and temperature cooperate to destabilize the dimeric form of the pE, a fundamental step that enables the formation of the fusion-active trimer, remains unclear. Here, we investigate this synergy for Dengue serotypes of greatest medical relevance, DENV-2 and DENV-3. All-atom molecular dynamics simulations were performed on the microsecond scale, at 28 °C, 37 °C, and 40 °C under pH 5, 6, and 7 using CHARMM36m force fields and complemented by extended coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations for the DENV-2 system at 37 °C and pH 5, and for the DENV-3 system at 28 °C and pH 5, and at 37 °C and pH 7. Our simulations suggest that increasing the temperature from 28 to 37 °C tends to expand the conformational space at neutral pH, potentially weakening dimer integrity through modulation of the interfacial interaction network. Acidification appears to amplify this effect in a serotype-specific manner: in our simulations DENV-2 required pH 5, while DENV-3 responded at pH 6. Additionally, distance and principal component analyses revealed an asymmetric dissociation pathway, termed the "compensatory embrace", observed in both all-atom and coarse-grained models. Structural analyses further highlighted the differences in histidine distribution between the serotypes. Moreover, interaction mapping at 37 °C identified candidate interfacial contacts that may act as pH-sensitive latches, maintaining stability at pH 7 but breaking upon acidification. Collectively, these results suggest a potential hierarchy of physicochemical triggers that may contribute to the conversion of dimer into fusion-competent monomers. These interfacial hotspots and the "compensatory embrace" constitute structurally informed targets that, pending validation under native virion conditions, may guide the rational design of antivirals and immunogens, underscoring the value of long-time scale molecular dynamics simulations as a hypothesis-generating tool in drug discovery.
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨pH和温度对登革病毒DENV-2和DENV-3包膜糖蛋白(pE)二聚体形式的协同效应,这对于形成融合活性三聚体至关重要。登革病毒发病机制依赖于由低pH诱导的pE构象重排,但pH和温度如何协同作用的机制仍不清楚。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究使用CHARMM36m力场,在不同温度(28 °C、37 °C、40 °C)和pH值(5、6、7)条件下,对DENV-2和DENV-3进行了微秒级的分子动力学模拟。此外,还在特定条件下对DENV-2和DENV-3进行了扩展的粗粒度分子动力学模拟。
elements_zh.methods: 进行了微秒级的全原子分子动力学模拟,并在特定条件下对DENV-2和DENV-3进行了扩展的粗粒度分子动力学模拟。模拟使用CHARMM36m力场进行。
elements_zh.main_results: 模拟结果表明,温度从28 °C升高到37 °C会扩大中性pH下的构象空间,可能削弱二聚体的完整性。酸化以血清型特异性方式放大了这一效应,DENV-2需要pH 5,而DENV-3则在pH 6时产生反应。距离和主成分分析揭示了一条不对称的解离路径,称为"补偿性拥抱"。结构分析突出了不同血清型之间组氨酸分布的差异,相互作用图谱识别了候选的界面接触点,这些接触点可能作为pH敏感的闩锁。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些结果总体上表明可能存在一种物理化学触发因素的层次结构,这可能有助于二聚体向融合活性单体的转化。这些界面热点和"补偿性拥抱"构成了结构信息指导的目标,可用于抗病毒药物和免疫原的合理设计。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为理解登革病毒和发病机制的分子机制提供了见解,并可能指导抗病毒药物和免疫原的合理设计,强调了在药物发现中长时尺度分子动力学模拟作为假设生成工具的价值。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于使用了分子动力学模拟,这些是计算模型,可能无法完全捕捉病毒的所有行为。研究结果仅适用于所测试的条件,可能无法推广到所有生理条件。模拟是在受控条件下进行的,可能无法完全代表原生病毒颗粒环境的复杂性。

title_zh: pH和温度对登革病毒包膜二聚体的协同效应:来自微秒分子动力学模拟的见解。
source_body_en: Dengue pathogenesis depends on a conformational rearrangement of the envelope glycoprotein (pE) induced by low pH. However, how pH and temperature cooperate to destabilize the dimeric form of the pE, a fundamental step that enables the formation of the fusion-active trimer, remains unclear. Here, we investigate this synergy for Dengue serotypes of greatest medical relevance, DENV-2 and DENV-3. All-atom molecular dynamics simulations were performed on the microsecond scale, at 28 °C, 37 °C, and 40 °C under pH 5, 6, and 7 using CHARMM36m force fields and complemented by extended coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations for the DENV-2 system at 37 °C and pH 5, and for the DENV-3 system at 28 °C and pH 5, and at 37 °C and pH 7. Our simulations suggest that increasing the temperature from 28 to 37 °C tends to expand the conformational space at neutral pH, potentially weakening dimer integrity through modulation of the interfacial interaction network. Acidification appears to amplify this effect in a serotype-specific manner: in our simulations DENV-2 required pH 5, while DENV-3 responded at pH 6. Additionally, distance and principal component analyses revealed an asymmetric dissociation pathway, termed the "compensatory embrace", observed in both all-atom and coarse-grained models. Structural analyses further highlighted the differences in histidine distribution between the serotypes. Moreover, interaction mapping at 37 °C identified candidate interfacial contacts that may act as pH-sensitive latches, maintaining stability at pH 7 but breaking upon acidification. Collectively, these results suggest a potential hierarchy of physicochemical triggers that may contribute to the conversion of dimer into fusion-competent monomers. These interfacial hotspots and the "compensatory embrace" constitute structurally informed targets that, pending validation under native virion conditions, may guide the rational design of antivirals and immunogens, underscoring the value of long-time scale molecular dynamics simulations as a hypothesis-generating tool in drug discovery.
abstract_zh: 登革病毒发病机制依赖于由低pH诱导的包膜糖蛋白(pE)构象重排。然而,pH和温度如何协同作用以破坏pE的二聚体形式,这是形成融合活性三聚体的基本步骤,目前仍不清楚。在此,我们研究了对登革热最具医学意义的DENV-2和DENV-3血清型中pH和温度的协同效应。使用CHARMM36m力场,在28 °C、37 °C和40 °C温度下,pH 5、6和7条件下进行了全原子分子动力学模拟。此外,对于DENV-2系统,在37 °C和pH 5条件下,以及DENV-3系统在28 °C和pH 5条件下,以及37 °C和pH 7条件下,还进行了扩展的粗粒度分子动力学模拟。我们的模拟结果表明,温度从28 °C升高到37 °C会扩大中性pH下的构象空间,可能通过调节界面相互作用网络而削弱二聚体的完整性。酸化似乎以血清型特异性方式放大了这一效应:在我们的模拟中,DENV-2需要pH 5,而DENV-3则在pH 6时产生反应。距离和主成分分析揭示了一条不对称的解离路径,称为"补偿性拥抱",在全原子和粗粒度模型中均观察到。结构分析进一步突出了不同血清型之间组氨酸分布的差异。此外,在37 °C条件下进行的相互作用图谱识别了候选的界面接触点,这些接触点可能作为pH敏感的闩锁,维持pH 7时的稳定性,但在酸化条件下会断裂。总体而言,这些结果表明可能存在一种物理化学触发因素的层次结构,这可能有助于二聚体向融合活性单体的转化。这些界面热点和"补偿性拥抱"构成了结构信息指导的目标,待在原生病毒颗粒条件下验证后,可能有助于抗病毒药物和免疫原的合理设计,强调了在药物发现中长时尺度分子动力学模拟作为假设生成工具的价值。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨pH和温度对登革病毒DENV-2和DENV-3包膜糖蛋白(pE)二聚体形式的协同效应,这对于形成融合活性三聚体至关重要。登革病毒发病机制依赖于由低pH诱导的pE构象重排,但pH和温度如何协同作用的机制仍不清楚。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究使用CHARMM36m力场,在不同温度(28 °C、37 °C、40 °C)和pH值(5、6、7)条件下,对DENV-2和DENV-3进行了微秒级的分子动力学模拟。此外,还在特定条件下对DENV-2和DENV-3进行了扩展的粗粒度分子动力学模拟。
analysis_zh.methods: 进行了微秒级的全原子分子动力学模拟,并在特定条件下对DENV-2和DENV-3进行了扩展的粗粒度分子动力学模拟。模拟使用CHARMM36m力场进行。
analysis_zh.main_results: 模拟结果表明,温度从28 °C升高到37 °C会扩大中性pH下的构象空间,可能削弱二聚体的完整性。酸化以血清型特异性方式放大了这一效应,DENV-2需要pH 5,而DENV-3则在pH 6时产生反应。距离和主成分分析揭示了一条不对称的解离路径,称为"补偿性拥抱"。结构分析突出了不同血清型之间组氨酸分布的差异,相互作用图谱识别了候选的界面接触点,这些接触点可能作为pH敏感的闩锁。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些结果总体上表明可能存在一种物理化学触发因素的层次结构,这可能有助于二聚体向融合活性单体的转化。这些界面热点和"补偿性拥抱"构成了结构信息指导的目标,可用于抗病毒药物和免疫原的合理设计。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为理解登革病毒和发病机制的分子机制提供了见解,并可能指导抗病毒药物和免疫原的合理设计,强调了在药物发现中长时尺度分子动力学模拟作为假设生成工具的价值。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于使用了分子动力学模拟,这些是计算模型,可能无法完全捕捉病毒的所有行为。研究结果仅适用于所测试的条件,可能无法推广到所有生理条件。模拟是在受控条件下进行的,可能无法完全代表原生病毒颗粒环境的复杂性。

title: Structure-Guided Design of a Subnanomolar Dengue Virus NS4B Inhibitor.
abstract: Dengue virus nonstructural protein 4B (NS4B) is an essential regulator of viral replication but remains structurally unresolved, limiting drug discovery. Here, we combine modeling, ligand-based design, and experimental validation to enable structure-guided inhibition of NS4B. Comparative models across all four serotypes reveal a conserved transmembrane binding pocket consistent with resistance mutations. Docking of JNJ-series inhibitors defines key interaction features that guide the development of predictive field-based 3D-QSAR models (R = 0.91, Q = 0.89). Prospective screening of bioisosteric and in-house compounds identifies BNJ-495 as a candidate broad-spectrum inhibitor with predicted activity across all four dengue serotypes. Experimental validation confirms potent activity against dengue virus serotype 2 (IC50 = 0.17 nM) with a high selectivity index (∼37,000). Conserved binding interactions across serotypes support broad-spectrum potential. This study establishes a general framework for targeting structurally elusive viral membrane proteins.
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling

abstract_zh: 登革病毒 非结构蛋白 4B(NS4B)是病毒复制的关键调节因子,但其结构尚未明确,限制了药物研发。在此研究中,我们结合建模、基于配体的设计和实验验证,实现了对 NS4B 的结构指导型抑制。通过比较所有四种血清型的模型,揭示了一个保守的跨膜结合口袋,与 突变 抗性相关。JNJ 系列抑制剂的对接分析定义了关键的相互作用特征,指导了预测性基于场的 3D-QSAR 模型的开发(R = 0.91,Q = 0.89)。对生物等排体和内部化合物的前瞻性筛选确定了 BNJ-495 作为具有预测活性的广谱抑制剂,可作用于所有四种登革病毒血清型。实验验证确认了其对 登革病毒 血清型 2 的强效活性(IC50 = 0.17 nM),并具有高选择性指数(约 37,000)。在不同血清型中保守的结合相互作用支持其广谱潜力。本研究建立了一个针对结构难以解析的病毒膜蛋白的通用框架。

title: Increasing dengue outbreaks in temperate Brazil are associated with Aedes aegypti invasion and infestation levels
abstract: Abstract Dengue fever, caused by dengue virus (DENV), is one of the most significant mosquito-borne diseases globally, with increasing risk due to the expansion of Aedes vectors into subtropical and temperate zones. Brazil accounted for 70% of dengue cases reported worldwide in 2024, and the virus has recently become endemic in the southernmost state of Rio Grande do Sul. Here, we integrate entomological, epidemiological and environmental data and generate complementary genomic data to investigate DENV dynamics in Southern Brazil from 2015 to 2023. During this period, Aedes aegypti expanded across state municipalities, with a marked increase in dengue cases from 2020 onward. Nearly half of the municipalities surpassed the incidence threshold of ≥20 cases per 100,000 residents per year by 2023, indicating endemic transmission. Genomic analysis of 665 new DENV genomes is consistent with the local persistence of viral lineages across years, driving seasonal outbreaks. Moreover, Northwest and Metropolitan regions are identified as key hubs for viral spread within the Rio Grande do Sul state. These findings highlight the north-to-south expansion of dengue into temperate regions, emphasizing the urgent need for intensification of vector control and surveillance in newly endemic areas to mitigate dengue burden in a mostly naive human population.

title: Dengue in a warming climate: lengthening transmission windows and ageing of reported cases in China's six highest-burden provincial-level administrative divisions, 2005–2020
abstract: Abstract Background Dengue has intensified in China over the past two decades, yet how the form of its epidemiology — the seasonal span of transmission and the age structure of cases — has changed remains unquantified with long, age-stratified subnational series. We examined sixteen years of surveillance from China's six highest-burden provincial-level administrative divisions (PLADs) against the backdrop of a warming climate. Methods Monthly, age-stratified counts of reported dengue cases and deaths (2005–2020) were obtained from the Public Health Science Data Center of the Chinese CDC for Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Yunnan and Zhejiang — the six Category I (highest-risk) PLADs of the national guideline. For each PLAD-year we counted months with ≥ 1 reported case (transmission window). The change in the proportion of cases aged ≥ 60 years between 2005–2012 and 2013–2019 was decomposed into population-structure and age-specific-rate effects using Kitagawa–Das Gupta decomposition with Shapley averaging, with yearly interpolated provincial population denominators. Provincial climate series (2005–2022) were aggregated from the CN05.1 gridded observations (0.25°); thermally suitable months (monthly mean temperature ≥ 15°C) and winter-margin indicators were trend-tested. title: Clinical and hematological profile and outcomes of children with dengue infection: a prospective observational study
abstract: Background: Dengue is an important cause of morbidity among children in tropical countries, with clinical manifestations ranging from a self-limiting febrile illness to severe dengue associated with plasma leakage, shock, and organ dysfunction. Early identification of children at risk of severe disease is essential for prompt management and improved outcomes. The present study aimed to evaluate the clinical and hematological profile of pediatric dengue infection and determine its association with disease severity and clinical outcomes. Methods: This prospective observational study was conducted in the Department of Pediatrics at a rural tertiary-care teaching hospital in Maharashtra, India, between September 2022 and February 2024. A total of 195 children aged 0-13 years with laboratory-confirmed dengue infection (positive NS1 antigen and/or dengue IgM antibody) were enrolled consecutively. Patients were classified according to the World Health Organization (WHO) 2009 dengue classification into dengue fever (DF), dengue fever with warning signs (DFWS), and severe dengue. Clinical characteristics, laboratory parameters, treatment received, duration of hospitalization, and outcomes were analyzed. Results: Out of the 195 children, 156 (80.0%) had DF, 28 (14.4%) had DFWS, and 11 (5.6%) had severe dengue. Increasing age was significantly associated with disease severity (p<0.05), whereas sex distribution was comparable across groups (p=0.81). Bleeding manifestations (p<0.001), nausea/vomiting (p<0.001), abdominal pain (p<0.001), myalgia (p=0.013), hepatomegaly (p=0.001), ascites (p=0.001), and shock (p<0.001) were significantly associated with severe disease. Progressive thrombocytopenia, lower nadir platelet count, higher total leukocyte count, and increased highest packed cell volume were significantly associated with disease severity (all p<0.05). NS1 antigen positivity showed a significant association with severe disease (p<0.01), whereas dengue IgM positivity did not (p=0.56). Increasing disease severity was associated with greater requirements for intravenous fluids, plasma transfusion, platelet transfusion, inotropic support, and longer hospital stay (all p<0.01). All children recovered, and no mortality was observed. Conclusions: Older age, gastrointestinal symptoms, bleeding manifestations, hepatomegaly, ascites, shock, thrombocytopenia, leukocytosis, and elevated packed cell volume were significantly associated with severe dengue in children. Careful clinical assessment together with serial hematological monitoring remains essential for early recognition of severe dengue and timely institution of supportive management, contributing to favorable clinical outcomes.

title: Myopericarditis Manifestation in Post-Dengue Infection Pediatric Patient in Endemic Country: Case Report
abstract: Background: Myopericarditis is one of the serious complications of severe dengue manifestations. The increased risk of myopericarditis in severe dengue cases may be associated with the immune system’s overactivity. Dengue myocarditis has a higher prevalence in the pediatric population than in adults. Case Illustration: An 11-year-old boy presented with heart failure syndrome after a recent dengue fever infection. Laboratory test results showed increased Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR) and serum Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), with a slight increase of serum troponin. Echocardiography and Cardiac Magnetic Resonance (CMR) studies confirm myocardial and pericardial involvement. Post-dengue myopericarditis diagnosis was made, and the patient was administered anti-heart failure medication and oral corticosteroid therapy. The patient improved after one month of therapy, as shown by the evaluation of laboratory and imaging criteria. Conclusions: Myocarditis should be considered if one of the classic triad of myocarditis, such as chest pain, congestive heart failure, and/or arrhythmia, develops in a recent viral infection history. These phenomena suggest that the clinician consider and have a high index of suspicion toward latent complications of post-dengue myocardial and pericardial inflammation syndrome. Hence, early diagnosis and long-term longitudinal surveillance studies are of the utmost importance in dengue-induced myopericarditis, especially in the dengue-endemic area, in order to prevent myocardial remodeling progression to dilated cardiomyopathy.

title: Clinical profile, serological patterns and treatment outcomes of dengue fever: a prospective cohort study at a tertiary care university hospital
abstract: Background: Dengue fever, a globally significant mosquito borne viral infection, exhibits a wide spectrum of clinical manifestations, yet gender specific variations in its presentation and outcomes remain underexplored. We conducted a prospective observational study at Jaipur National University Institute for Medical Sciences and Research Centre, enrolling 50 confirmed dengue patients to evaluate demographic, clinical, and serological differences between genders. Methods: The cohort comprised 62% females and 38% males, with fever (90%), generalized weakness (54%), and myalgia (44%) as the most common symptoms. Hematological involvement was predominant (92%), followed by hepatic (54%) and respiratory (28%) systems. Serological analysis revealed IgM as the most detected marker (50%), while thrombocytopenia (92%) and hepatomegaly (34%) were frequent comorbidities. Results: Notably, gender-based differences emerged, with females exhibiting significantly higher IgG seropositivity (p=0.026) and lower hemoglobin levels (p=0.011) compared to males. Treatment regimens were largely supportive, including pantoprazole (98%), paracetamol (84%), and ondansetron (66%). Our findings highlight the critical role of early hematological and serological monitoring in identifying severe cases, while underscoring the need for gender specific considerations in dengue management. Conclusions: The study provides novel insights into the interplay between gender and disease manifestations, offering actionable evidence to refine clinical protocols and public health strategies in endemic regions. These results emphasize the importance of tailored interventions to mitigate complications and improve patient outcomes.

title: Sporadic detection of dengue virus RNA in California wastewater solids
abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) is the most prevalent mosquito-borne virus globally, endemic in over 100 countries and associated with around 40,000 deaths each year. Prior research has shown that DENV RNA can be detected in wastewater, but detection rates vary widely depending on the setting and method used. In this study, we analyzed 1,072 untreated wastewater samples from five treatment plants in California, collected between December 2023 and December 2025, to evaluate wastewater-based surveillance for DENV. We compared wastewater data with reported clinical incidence and Aedes aegypti mosquito abundance measurements over the same period collected by the California Department of Public Health. DENV RNA was found in 1.2% of wastewater samples (13/1,072). DENV-1 was most common (0.6%, 6/1,072), followed by DENV-2 (0.4%, 4/1,072), and DENV-4 (0.3%, 3/1,072). No DENV-3 RNA was detected. DENV RNA was detected only in wastewater from southern California (plants in Los Angeles and San Diego counties), with no detections in wastewater from the Bay Area, including plants located in San Jose and Oakland. There was no correlation between wastewater DENV RNA levels and county-wide reported dengue incidence during the same week. However, counties with a higher incidence over the study period showed greater detection frequency of DENV RNA in wastewater. aegypti abundance was correlated with weekly incidence of locally-transmitted cases (Spearman's {rho}=0.45, p<0.01). Our results indicate that wastewater surveillance can detect DENV in areas of higher incidence, but the low detection frequency and sporadic nature of positive samples limit its utility as a standalone surveillance approach. Given the low incidence of dengue in California and the presence of robust clinical and mosquito surveillance systems, wastewater monitoring does not currently add significant public health value for dengue surveillance in the state.

title: Chinese expert consensus on the diagnosis and treatment of severe dengue
abstract: Abstract Severe dengue (SD), characterized by rapid progression and high mortality risk, poses a major challenge to clinical practice and public health prevention and control. In China, unlike in some highly endemic regions abroad, SD primarily affects older patients and those with underlying comorbidities. To standardize the clinical diagnosis and management of SD in China, an expert group developed the Chinese Expert Consensus on the Diagnosis and Treatment of Severe Dengue based on a systematic literature search and expert discussions. The document elaborates on the definition and mechanisms of SD and recommends diagnostic criteria, warning signs, and therapeutic strategies tailored to the Chinese clinical context. It aims to improve clinicians’ capacity for the early recognition of and timely intervention for SD, thereby reducing mortality and advancing the overall standard of SD diagnosis and treatment in China.

title: Epidemiological Effectiveness and Long-Term Sustainability of Wolbachia-Based Biocontrol for Dengue Reduction in Latin America: A Systematic Review Protocol
abstract: Dengue virus transmission presents a severe public health challenge across endemic urban areas of Latin America, where conventional vector control methods such as insecticide fogging, chemical larviciding, and routine source reduction are increasingly constrained by insecticide resistance and operational limits. Biological vector control utilizing field releases of Wolbachia-infected Aedes aegypti mosquitoes has emerged as a promising strategy to inhibit viral replication and decrease human dengue incidence; however, significant variations in strain introgression durability across Latin American cities and unanswered questions regarding multi-modal integration with dengue vaccines or ecological impacts on non-target vectors highlight the urgent need for a synthesized evidence base. This systematic literature review aims to systematically evaluate and synthesize primary empirical field evidence on the epidemiological effectiveness of Wolbachia-infected mosquito releases compared to conventional vector control in reducing human dengue incidence, case counts, and viral transmission rates across urban endemic settings in Latin America, while simultaneously identifying the operational, environmental, and ecological factors that determine long-term intervention sustainability. Specifically, this review addresses how effective Wolbachia deployments are relative to standard control baselines and examines how operational co-deployments, environmental conditions, and strain fixation durability influence long-term efficacy. Ultimately, this project expects to deliver quantitative pooled or narrative estimates of dengue incidence reduction, provide insights into optimal release protocols and community engagement, evaluate long-term strain durability under chemical control stress, and offer evidence-based recommendations to optimize Integrated Vector Management (IVM) frameworks for public health authorities across Latin America.

source_records.abstract: Dengue virus transmission presents a severe public health challenge across endemic urban areas of Latin America, where conventional vector control methods such as insecticide fogging, chemical larviciding, and routine source reduction are increasingly constrained by insecticide resistance and operational limits. Biological vector control utilizing field releases of Wolbachia-infected Aedes aegypti mosquitoes has emerged as a promising strategy to inhibit viral replication and decrease human dengue incidence; however, significant variations in strain introgression durability across Latin American cities and unanswered questions regarding multi-modal integration with dengue vaccines or ecological impacts on non-target vectors highlight the urgent need for a synthesized evidence base. This systematic literature review aims to systematically evaluate and synthesize primary empirical field evidence on the epidemiological effectiveness of Wolbachia-infected mosquito releases compared to conventional vector control in reducing human dengue incidence, case counts, and viral transmission rates across urban endemic settings in Latin America, while simultaneously identifying the operational, environmental, and ecological factors that determine long-term intervention sustainability. Specifically, this review addresses how effective Wolbachia deployments are relative to standard control baselines and examines how operational co-deployments, environmental conditions, and strain fixation durability influence long-term efficacy. Ultimately, this project expects to deliver quantitative pooled or narrative estimates of dengue incidence reduction, provide insights into optimal release protocols and community engagement, evaluate long-term strain durability under chemical control stress, and offer evidence-based recommendations to optimize Integrated Vector Management (IVM) frameworks for public health authorities across Latin America.

title: An outbreak investigation of a large dengue fever outbreak in Somaliland, 2023–2024
abstract: Somaliland experienced a large dengue fever outbreak between 2023 and 2024. National laboratory surveillance identified 4971 clinically suspected cases that underwent testing (‘tested probable cases’), of which 1703 were confirmed using rapid diagnostic tests. Three deaths were reported. Cases spanned five regions of Somaliland, with 74% in Marodijeh. As surveillance data were restricted to public-sector facilities, these findings represent a lower-bound estimate of true dengue transmission. Contribution: We highlight the utility of the new laboratory surveillance and the need for mitigating dengue risks amid climatic fluctuations.
journal: Journal of Public Health in Africa

title: Antiviral Strategies Against Dengue Virus: Viral Targets, Host Pathways, and Chinese Herbal Medicines
abstract: Dengue is caused by four antigenically distinct dengue virus serotypes (DENV-1 to DENV-4) and remains a major global public health threat. It is endemic in more than 100 countries and territories, primarily in tropical and subtropical regions. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), approximately 390 million DENV infections occur annually, with nearly half of the world’s population at risk of infection. Complex virus–host interactions and disease mechanisms continue to complicate antiviral development. No dengue-specific antiviral therapy has been approved. This review summarizes recent advances in anti-DENV therapeutics, including inhibitors targeting viral proteins, host factors, and virus–host interactions. In addition, it highlights the antiviral potential of Chinese herbal medicines and their bioactive compounds, and discusses priorities for their further development.

title: A case-control study to determine the risk factors of dengue infections in endemic dengue area in Yemen
abstract: Background and aims: The effectiveness of dengue prevention in a subtropical nation such as Yemen, where the climate encourages the establishment of Aedes mosquito vectors, mostly rests on the accurate identification and management of risk factors. Thus, the purpose of this study was to investigate potential risk variables and how they relate to dengue infection.Methods: The study included 73 dengue patients (cases) and 146 controls (non-dengue patients admitted to other departments of the same hospitals: Al-Thawra General Hospital, Al-Amal Al-Arabi Hospital, and Al Hodeida Hospital in Al-Hodeida City, during the period from October 2024 to May 2025). Data were collected from the cases and controls by a standard questionnaire of dengue infection risk factors.Results: Differences in the risk of dengue virus infection were not observed between sexes. However, significant associations were found in the age groups: children under five years had an odds ratio of 3.6 (CI: 1.5 9.1, x2: 9.7, p: 0.001), and the 26–40 year age group had an odds ratio of 2.2 (CI: 1.1–4.5, x2: 5.4, p: 0.009). Statistically significant associations were found between various risk factors and dengue fever infection. These include sleeping without mosquito nets (probability ratio 2.7), exposure to stored water tanks (4.6), wearing short-sleeved clothing (8.3), the presence of swamps and sewage (3.9), vegetation around homes (4.8), and keeping windows/doors open (7.0). All associations had a p-value of less than 0.001, demonstrating strong statistical significance.Conclusions: Particularly in urban regions with high infection rates, these findings can aid in the creation of focused intervention tactics and public health awareness messages, such as encouraging personal preventive measures and community awareness campaigns. However, to improve the generalizability of these findings and their applicability to public policy, more study with bigger samples in various geographic, social, and environmental contexts is required.

title: A regression and value perception dual model for individual protection against Dengue
abstract: Dengue fever is an acute infectious disease transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, posing a threat to public health. As vaccines are not widely available, non-pharmacological interventions and behavioral improvements have become key prevention and control strategies. Based on the 8-year environmental and epidemic data of Guangzhou from 2015 to 2022, a regression model was constructed to explore the effects of Aedes density, climate, and population density on dengue fever infection rate. A value perception model was established, and the subjective infection probability, the effectiveness of prevention and control measures, and the perception of health loss are the core psychological variables that drive individual protection behavior. A sequentially coupled regression and value perception dual-model framework was then constructed. In this framework, the regression model identifies aggregate environmental risk signals associated with dengue infection rates, while the value perception model uses these signals as scenario inputs for analysing subjective infection probability, perceived health loss, perceived effectiveness of protective measures, and perceived protection cost. A three-dimensional comprehensive prevention and control strategy of vector regulation, behavioral intervention, and medical response was proposed. Through theoretical scenario simulation and sensitivity analysis, the study identified how changes in subjective infection probability, perceived effectiveness of protective measures, and perceived health loss may influence individual protective tendency. The proposed sequentially coupled dual-model framework provides an interpretable approach for linking environmental risk identification with behavioural decision analysis, and its transformation into behavioral decision-making and provides evidence-based and targeted strategies for urban dengue fever prevention and control and public health practice.

title: Higher late galectin-3 and galectin-9 amid lower cytokine concentrations in DENV-2-exposed PBMC cultures from older versus middle-aged donors
abstract: Older adults with dengue have higher risks of adverse outcomes, but the contribution of age-related immune responses remains uncertain. We compared soluble mediators after ex vivo dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV-2) exposure of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from older and middle-aged volunteer donors. PBMCs from 10 older donors (≥ 65 years; median age, 74.9 years; observed range, 65.8–92.0 years) and 10 middle-aged donors (20–64 years eligible; median age, 39.4 years; observed range, 34.8–49.1 years) were exposed to DENV-2 strain TH-36 at a multiplicity of infection of 5. Supernatants collected before exposure and at 24, 48, and 72 h were assayed for GM-CSF, IFN-γ, IL-6, IL-10, MCP-1, TNF-α, VEGF-A, galectin-3, and galectin-9. Between-group p values at each time point were unadjusted exploratory comparisons. Compared with middle-aged donor cultures, older donor cultures had higher galectin-3 concentrations at 48 and 72 h (median 363.6 versus 197.8 pg/mL, p = 0.0412; 810.1 versus 218.5 pg/mL, p = 0.0011) and higher galectin-9 at 72 h (219.6 versus 92.23 pg/mL, p = 0.0355). Concentrations of the seven other measured mediators were generally lower in older donor cultures at 24–72 h. IFN-γ, IL-10, and TNF-α also differed at baseline. Interpretation of the nominal p values is limited by the small sample and multiple comparisons. After ex vivo DENV-2 exposure, PBMC cultures from older donors had higher galectin-3 and galectin-9 concentrations at selected late time points and generally lower concentrations of the seven other measured mediators than cultures from predominantly middle-aged donors. This contrasting pattern highlights the value of examining galectins alongside other soluble mediators when investigating variation in responses to DENV-2. The small sample and culture model limit causal and clinical inference, and cytokine–galectin associations were not tested. Larger donor-linked experiments and studies in patients with dengue are needed to assess reproducibility and clinical relevance.

title: Impacto epidemiológico del dengue y del chikungunya en zonas urbanas: revisión sistemática Epidemiological impact of dengue and chikungunya in urban areas: a systematic review
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre el impacto epidemiológico urbano del dengue y del chikungunya. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios. Resultados: la incidencia mundial del dengue aumentó desde 1990, con diferencias regionales marcadas y alta carga en América Latina. El chikungunya se expandió por las Américas desde 2013 y produjo brotes urbanos explosivos, con manifestaciones articulares persistentes. La urbanización, la expansión de Aedes aegypti y Aedes albopictus y la resistencia a insecticidas favorecieron la transmisión. Destacan como estrategias las nuevas vacunas y el control vectorial integrado. Conclusión: ambas arbovirosis son una carga creciente para las ciudades tropicales y subtropicales y exigen vigilancia y control sostenidos.

title: Estrategias de prevención del dengue en comunidades urbanas: revisión sistemática Dengue prevention strategies in urban communities: a systematic review
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre la efectividad de las estrategias de prevención del dengue en comunidades urbanas y su aplicabilidad al contexto ecuatoriano. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: revisiones sistemáticas con y sin metaanálisis, estudios en Ecuador, intervenciones comunitarias y una evaluación económica. Resultados: el control químico aislado redujo los índices entomológicos sin efecto demostrado sobre la transmisión. El manejo ambiental con participación comunitaria, las mallas en las viviendas y las cubiertas de recipientes mostraron los resultados más favorables. El almacenamiento de agua, la percepción del riesgo y la falta de servicios básicos condicionaron la prevención en Ecuador. Conclusión: la prevención del dengue urbano requiere estrategias integradas, comunitarias y sostenidas, con vigilancia epidemiológica y mejoras de los servicios básicos.

title: Environmental and Entomological Determinants of Dengue Transmission in Arid and Semi-Arid Rajasthan, India: Implications for Public Health Risk Management
abstract: Background: Dengue transmission is increasingly recognized in environments that are traditionally considered less favourable for sustained Aedes mosquito proliferation. Rajasthan contains extensive arid and semi-arid landscapes where seasonal water availability, domestic water storage and climatic variability may create localized ecological conditions favourable for dengue transmission. Objective: The present study examined dengue occurrence in selected arid and semi-arid districts of Rajasthan and evaluated environmental and entomological characteristics relevant to Aedes aegypti persistence in a semi-arid setting. Materials and Methods: Retrospective dengue surveillance data were compiled for six districts of Rajasthan during 2015–2019, comprising arid districts (Jaisalmer, Barmer and Bikaner) and semi-arid districts (Jodhpur, Sri Ganganagar and Hanumangarh). In addition, entomological observations were undertaken in domestic and peri-domestic settings in Jodhpur. Climatic observations and laboratory surveillance data from the broader research programme were considered to interpret seasonal transmission. Aedes breeding habitats were documented, with particular attention to water-storage containers, tanks and other artificial receptacles. Results: A total of 5,142 dengue cases were recorded across the selected districts during 2015–2019, of which 3,785 occurred in the semi-arid group. Jaisalmer and Jodhpur showed the highest reported incidence within the arid and semi-arid groups, respectively, whereas Bikaner and Hanumangarh showed the lowest incidence in their respective groups. Entomological observations demonstrated the persistence of Aedes aegypti in domestic and peri-domestic habitats despite the semi-arid environmental conditions. Water-storage containers, tanks and artificial receptacles represented important breeding environments. The broader Jodhpur investigation further demonstrated seasonal dengue peaks during the post-monsoon period and associations with temperature and relative humidity. Conclusion: Dengue transmission in arid and semi-arid Rajasthan is supported by the interaction of seasonal environmental conditions and anthropogenic water-storage practices that provide breeding opportunities for Aedes aegypti. Public-health risk management in such environments should integrate climatic surveillance with targeted inspection and management of domestic and peri-domestic water-holding habitats.

title: Comparative analysis of serum antibody responses and immune landscapes in patients with acute DENV-1, DENV-2, and Chikungunya virus infections
abstract: Introduction Dengue virus (DENV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV) are major mosquito-borne arboviruses that increasingly co-circulate in tropical and subtropical regions, including southern China. However, the extent to which these viruses induce shared or distinct host immune responses remains poorly understood. This study aimed to comparatively characterize immune responses during acute DENV-1, DENV-2, and CHIKV infections. Materials and methods A total of 80 serum samples were analyzed, including 65 samples from patients with laboratory-confirmed DENV-1 (n = 29), DENV-2 (n = 10), or CHIKV (n = 26) infections and 15 healthy controls.Viral RNA was detected by real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction. Virus-specific IgM and IgG responses were measured by Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay, and serum cytokines were quantified using a multiplex assay. Group comparisons used nonparametric tests, and associations among antibody responses, cytokine concentrations, and viral RNA levels were assessed using Spearman’s rank correlation. Multiple comparisons were adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure. Results The three infections shared features of interferon-associated immune activation and relatively restrained systemic inflammation but exhibited distinct immune mediator profiles, characterized by differential inflammatory mediator and growth factor responses. After multiple-testing correction, cytokine–cytokine correlation analysis revealed both shared and infection-specific patterns of immune mediator covariation, with shared associations involving IL-9, TNF-β, CCL4, and CXCL1 across all three infection groups. Positive associations between pathogen-specific IgM responses and Ct values were observed across the infections, although the association was not statistically significant for DENV-2 after multiple-testing correction. IgG responses showed a similar association only in DENV-1 infection. Integration of cytokine and antibody profiles further revealed distinct immune association patterns: DENV-1 showed broader associations involving viral RNA levels, inflammatory mediators, and humoral responses, whereas CHIKV displayed a more restricted pattern centered on associations between inflammatory mediators and IgM responses. Discussion These findings reveal shared and distinct immune responses during acute DENV-1, DENV-2, and CHIKV infections and provide a comparative framework for investigating virus-associated immune regulation during acute arboviral infections.

title: PREVENÇÃO DA DENGUE NA ESTRATÉGIA SAÚDE DA FAMÍLIA NO BRASIL: INTEGRAÇÃO TERRITORIAL, EDUCAÇÃO EM SAÚDE E VIGILÂNCIA DENGUE PREVENTION IN THE FAMILY HEALTH STRATEGY IN BRAZIL: TERRITORIAL INTEGRATION, HEALTH EDUCATION AND SURVEILLANCE PREVENCIÓN DEL DENGUE EN LA ESTRATEGIA SALUD DE LA FAMILIA EN BRASIL: INTEGRACIÓN TERRITORIAL, EDUCACIÓN EN SALUD Y VIGILANCIA
abstract: Objetivo: analisar criticamente as evidências brasileiras recentes sobre a contribuição da Estratégia Saúde da Família (ESF) e da Atenção Primária à Saúde (APS) para a prevenção da dengue, com ênfase na articulação entre profissionais, educação em saúde e vigilância territorial. Método: revisão crítica estruturada, baseada em protocolo previamente elaborado para o período 2020–2026 e em consulta dirigida a publicações científicas disponíveis em PubMed e SciELO, sem pretensão de exaustividade. Resultados: as seis publicações centrais examinadas descrevem fragmentação entre equipes de Saúde da Família e vigilância, educação em saúde predominantemente verticalizada, integração viável, porém com ajustes necessários, entre agentes de combate às endemias e a ESF, e potencial dos registros assistenciais para antecipar alertas de surtos. Um estudo nacional identificou antecipação de alertas em parte dos surtos detectados pela vigilância convencional, sem avaliar redução causal da transmissão. Conclusão: a integração entre APS, vigilância e comunidade constitui uma direção organizacional promissora, mas a evidência disponível nesta síntese não permite estimar o efeito das estratégias sobre a incidência de dengue. Estudos de implementação e avaliações comparativas são necessários.

source_records.abstract: Objetivo: analisar criticamente as evidências brasileiras recentes sobre a contribuição da Estratégia Saúde da Família (ESF) e da Atenção Primária à Saúde (APS) para a prevenção da dengue, com ênfase na articulação entre profissionais, educação em saúde e vigilância territorial. Método: revisão crítica estruturada, baseada em protocolo previamente elaborado para o período 2020–2026 e em consulta dirigida a publicações científicas disponíveis em PubMed e SciELO, sem pretensão de exaustividade. Resultados: as seis publicações centrais examinadas descrevem fragmentação entre equipes de Saúde da Família e vigilância, educação em saúde predominantemente verticalizada, integração viável, porém com ajustes necessários, entre agentes de combate às endemias e a ESF, e potencial dos registros assistenciais para antecipar alertas de surtos. Um estudo nacional identificou antecipação de alertas em parte dos surtos detectados pela vigilância convencional, sem avaliar redução causal da transmissão. Conclusão: a integração entre APS, vigilância e comunidade constitui uma direção organizacional promissora, mas a evidência disponível nesta síntese não permite estimar o efeito das estratégias sobre a incidência de dengue. Estudos de implementação e avaliações comparativas são necessários.

title: Health Promotion for Wolbachia-Based Dengue Control: A Scoping Review of Regulatory Readiness, Community Engagement, and Communication Strategies
abstract: Introduction: Wolbachia-based interventions have emerged as an effective strategy for reducing dengue transmission in endemic countries. However, successful implementation depends on comprehensive pre-release preparation, and evidence describing these preparatory models has not been synthesised systematically. This scoping review aimed to map and synthesise preparation models for Wolbachia-based dengue control programmes across dengue-endemic countries, focusing on regulatory preparation, community engagement, and communication strategies that facilitate community acceptance and successful implementation. Methods: Following PRISMA-ScR and Population–Concept–Context frameworks, we systematically searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Taylor & Francis for 2014 to 2025 publications describing Wolbachia pre-release processes in Asia, Latin America, Oceania, and Africa. All study designs reporting regulatory preparation, mosquito production/logistics, community engagement, and communication strategies were included. Data were extracted using standardised forms and synthesised narratively and thematically. Results: Of the 848 identified studies, 13 met the inclusion criteria. The review results identified three interacting Wolbachia programme preparations: regulatory preparation, community engagement, and communication. These domains were associated with mechanisms such as institutional legitimacy, dialogue, trust-building, informed participation, and context-sensitive communication that may support implementation readiness and community acceptance. Conclusion: The review suggests that Wolbachia programme preparation may support community acceptance through interconnected mechanisms of institutional legitimacy, dialogue, trust-building, informed participation, community-based structures, and context-sensitive communication, although these mechanisms may vary across social and regulatory contexts. These findings provide guiding principles for future Wolbachia-based dengue control programmes in diverse settings. This framework provides practical guidance for policymakers and public health practitioners seeking to strengthen community acceptance and support sustainable deployment of Wolbachia in dengue-endemic settings.

title: A Methodological Framework for Epidemiological Data Analysis: Dengue as a Model for Disease Surveillance and a One Health Perspective
abstract: Zoonotic and vector-borne diseases remain important public health problems, especially in regions where social, environmental, and epidemiological conditions favor their occurrence and spread. Transparent procedures for data organization, analysis, and interpretation are essential for translating epidemiological findings into public health information. In this context, dengue is an important model for epidemiological surveillance because its occurrence across diverse geographic settings involves seasonal patterns and demographic and environmental factors. Here, we propose a practical and structured framework for epidemiological data analysis in vector-borne diseases that can be applied to zoonotic diseases. We provide a step-by-step guide to organizing data, selecting descriptive and analytical methods, and interpreting results, using dengue as a model for disease surveillance and a One Health perspective. The framework is divided into five parts: (1) defining study scope and design, (2) conducting descriptive analysis, (3) examining association analyses of sociodemographic and clinical variables, (4) fitting multivariable analysis to integrate human and environmental data, and (5) performing statistical analysis through a step-by-step protocol. It combines dengue notification data with meteorological records to illustrate analyses at individual and population levels, while distinguishing observational associations from causal conclusions. The protocol demonstrates the analytical procedures using a freely available, user-friendly statistical software. The concepts and methodological approaches presented here can be adapted to other diseases according to their data sources, outcomes, and epidemiological context, supporting the development of epidemiological studies for disease surveillance, prevention, and control.

title: DENGUE NO MARANHÃO: PICO DE NOTIFICAÇÕES E CONCENTRAÇÃO ENTRE ADULTOS DE 20 A 39 ANOS DENGUE IN MARANHÃO, BRAZIL: A PEAK IN NOTIFICATIONS AND CONCENTRATION AMONG ADULTS AGED 20 TO 39 YEARS DENGUE EN MARANHÃO, BRASIL: PICO DE NOTIFICACIONES Y CONCENTRACIÓN ENTRE ADULTOS DE 20 A 39 AÑOS
abstract: Objetivo: descrever a distribuição das notificações de dengue no Maranhão entre 2023 e 2025 segundo ano, sexo, faixa etária, raça/cor e trimestre gestacional. Métodos: estudo epidemiológico descritivo e retrospectivo, com dados secundários agregados do Sinan/DATASUS. Calcularam-se frequências absolutas, relativas e variação anual. Resultados: foram analisadas 22.030 notificações; 2024 concentrou 11.354 (51,5%) e apresentou aumento de 127,0% em relação a 2023, enquanto 2025 registrou 5.675. Mulheres corresponderam a 52,5%, adultos de 20-39 anos formaram o grupo mais frequente e pessoas pardas somaram 17.083 registros. Entre 245 notificações em gestantes com trimestre informado, 44,9% ocorreram no segundo trimestre. Conclusão: o volume excepcional de 2024 e a concentração entre adultos orientam o planejamento da vigilância, da assistência e da educação em saúde. A menor contagem de 2025 não demonstra, isoladamente, redução sustentada da transmissão.
journal: Revista Ibero-Americana de Humanidades, Ciências e Educação

source_records.abstract: Objetivo: descrever a distribuição das notificações de dengue no Maranhão entre 2023 e 2025 segundo ano, sexo, faixa etária, raça/cor e trimestre gestacional. Métodos: estudo epidemiológico descritivo e retrospectivo, com dados secundários agregados do Sinan/DATASUS. Calcularam-se frequências absolutas, relativas e variação anual. Resultados: foram analisadas 22.030 notificações; 2024 concentrou 11.354 (51,5%) e apresentou aumento de 127,0% em relação a 2023, enquanto 2025 registrou 5.675. Mulheres corresponderam a 52,5%, adultos de 20-39 anos formaram o grupo mais frequente e pessoas pardas somaram 17.083 registros. Entre 245 notificações em gestantes com trimestre informado, 44,9% ocorreram no segundo trimestre. Conclusão: o volume excepcional de 2024 e a concentração entre adultos orientam o planejamento da vigilância, da assistência e da educação em saúde. A menor contagem de 2025 não demonstra, isoladamente, redução sustentada da transmissão.

abstract: Background: Dengue is an important mosquito-borne viral disease in tropical and subtropical regions. Community participation, elimination of mosquito breeding sites, personal protection and early recognition of warning signs are important components of dengue prevention and control. title: ESTUDO ECOLÓGICO LONGITUDINAL DA DENGUE E DA COBERTURA DO SOLO COM REGISTROS DE ZIKA NA NOVA ALTA PAULISTA ENTRE 2015 E 2024 LONGITUDINAL ECOLOGICAL STUDY OF DENGUE AND LAND COVER WITH ZIKA RECORDS IN NOVA ALTA PAULISTA, BRAZIL, FROM 2015 TO 2024 ESTUDIO ECOLÓGICO LONGITUDINAL DEL DENGUE Y DE LA COBERTURA DEL SUELO CON REGISTROS DE ZIKA EN LA NOVA ALTA PAULISTA ENTRE 2015 Y 2024
abstract: Objetivo: Descrever a série municipal de notificações de dengue, estimar sua associação longitudinal com formação florestal e áreas alagadas e de água e caracterizar os registros de Zika na Nova Alta Paulista. Métodos: Estudo ecológico com 30 municípios e 300 observações município-ano (2015–2024). As notificações de dengue vieram do InfoDengue, a cobertura do solo do MapBiomas e os registros de Zika do SINAN (2016–2024). Ajustou-se regressão de Poisson com efeitos fixos de município e ano, população como offset e erros padrão agrupados por município; a binomial negativa NB2 foi análise de sensibilidade. Resultados: A mediana municipal da incidência notificada atingiu 11.732,3 por 100 mil habitantes em 2023. Por aumento de um ponto percentual da área municipal, a razão de taxas foi 1,20 para formação florestal (IC95%: 0,54–2,68; p=0,637) e 1,04 para áreas alagadas e de água (IC95%: 0,67–1,60; p=0,864). Houve 52 notificações de Zika, das quais 13 não descartadas, incluindo duas confirmadas; quatro notificações não descartadas ocorreram durante a gestação. Não houve registros em 2023–2024. Conclusão: As estimativas não ofereceram evidência estatística de associação na escala e no período estudados, mas seus intervalos não demonstram ausência de efeito. A pequena variação temporal da cobertura do solo e o confundimento não medido limitam a interpretação. Os registros de Zika exigem atenção à completude da classificação e ao acompanhamento das gestantes.

title: Development and Functional Testing of a Web Based Dengue Weather Alert Prototype with WhatsApp Notifications in Palu, Indonesia
abstract: Background: Weather information may support dengue preparedness, although software functionality alone cannot establish forecasting accuracy. Objectives: This study developed a web based weather alert prototype integrating meteorological data and WhatsApp notifications for dengue preparedness in Palu, Indonesia. Methods: Research and development followed the Analysis, Design, and Development phases of the ADDIE model from January 14 to February 4, 2026. CodeIgniter 4 and MySQL supported coordinate based weather retrieval through OpenWeather, data storage, user registration, and automated notifications. Results: The prototype covered 46 urban villages across eight districts. Nine functional testing categories were reported as successful, including website accessibility, geographic data, weather integration, storage, notifications, decision logic, registration, profile management, and interface responsiveness. However, detailed test inputs, execution counts, and notification delivery receipts were unavailable. The 22 day development period could not independently establish a complete 30 day rainfall dataset without historical records. Weather thresholds remained literature informed assumptions without local predictive validation. Conclusions: The prototype demonstrated preliminary software integration capabilities. Reproducible functional testing, rainfall data verification, governance safeguards, and independent epidemiological validation are required before operational implementation for dengue preparedness.

title: A pilot study on the impact of infection routes on disease progression and immune response by dengue infection in AG129 mice
abstract: AG129 mouse is a mouse model commonly utilised in the study of dengue pathogenesis using various viral inoculation routes. Different viral infection routes may elicit distinct host responses. This pilot study compares the development of dengue virus infection in AG129 mice via intraperitoneal and subcutaneous routes. AG129 mice were infected with dengue virus type 2 (DENV-2) via intraperitoneal or subcutaneous injection. Disease progression was monitored through daily body weight and morbidity scores for 14 days. Plasma viral RNA levels were quantified by reverse transcription-quantitative PCR. Plasma non-structural protein 1 (NS1) level was determined by dengue NS1 antigen- ELISA method. Platelet and blood differential counts were counted. Plasma cytokines were assessed on day 1, 3, 5, and 7 post-infection using multiplex immunoassay. Body weight loss was similar between groups until day 4 post-infection, where intraperitoneally infected mice showed greater loss. Morbidity signs were more pronounced in intraperitoneally infected mice from day 2 to 6 post-infection. Viremia levels detected by NS1 protein and viral RNA were similar between both routes. Intraperitoneal infection triggered an earlier increase in white blood cells and neutrophil counts, as well as earlier lymphocyte reduction and thrombocytopenia. Cytokine analysis revealed early elevations of seven cytokines in intraperitoneally infected mice. In contrast, subcutaneously infected mice showed higher levels of interferon-γ and interleukin-10. Intraperitoneal infection in AG129 mice with DENV-2 induced thrombocytopenia, earlier immune responses and transiently higher morbidity as compared to the subcutaneous route. Therefore, different routes of virus inoculation should be carefully considered in future experimental designs using the AG129 mouse model.

Intraperitoneal infection in AG129 mice with DENV-2 induced thrombocytopenia, earlier immune responses and transiently higher morbidity as compared to the subcutaneous route. Therefore, different routes of virus inoculation should be carefully considered in future experimental designs using the AG129 mouse model.

title: Nivel de conocimiento y prácticas preventivas sobre el dengue en adultos de un comité del distrito de Comas, Lima
abstract: Objetivo: Determinar la relación entre el nivel de conocimiento y las prácticas preventivas sobre el dengue en adultos del distrito de Comas, Lima. Materiales y métodos: Estudio de tipo básica, con enfoque cuantitativo, diseño no experimental, de corte transversal y alcance relacional, con una muestra de 104 adultos. Se utilizó un cuestionario para medir el conocimiento (α = 0,761) y una guía de observación para las prácticas preventivas (α = 0,881), con validez de contenido binomial p = 0,000 y p = 0,00025 respectivamente. Resultados: No existió relación estadísticamente significativa entre las variables (p = 0,058; r = -0,186). Conclusiones: Se concluye que el nivel de conocimiento no se asocia con las prácticas preventivas, evidenciando que la adopción de estas conductas depende de otros factores más allá del conocimiento.

title: A dengue sob uma perspectiva epidemiológica e sociodemográfica: uma análise sobre o estado de Minas Gerais
abstract: O contexto epidemiológico da dengue no Brasil caracteriza-se por oscilações entre períodos endêmicos e surtos epidêmicos, representando um desafio contínuo à saúde pública. Este estudo tem como objetivo geral analisar o perfil epidemiológico e sociodemográfico da dengue no estado de Minas Gerais, com ênfase no município de Uberlândia, a partir de evidências da literatura científica recente. Trata-se de uma pesquisa bibliográfica, de caráter descritivo e exploratório, realizada em bases de dados nacionais e internacionais. Os resultados indicam elevada incidência da doença em determinados períodos do ano, forte associação com fatores socioambientais, desigualdades regionais e impacto significativo sobre o Sistema Único de Saúde. Conclui-se que a dengue permanece como um importante problema de saúde pública em Minas Gerais, exigindo estratégias integradas de vigilância epidemiológica, controle vetorial e ações intersetoriais.

title: Determinants of orthoflavivirus tropism in humans: from cellular entry to organ-specific pathogenesis.
abstract: Orthoflaviviruses, including dengue virus, tick-borne encephalitis virus, West Nile virus, Zika virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, and yellow fever virus, cause a wide spectrum of diseases in humans despite sharing a similar genomic organization. These viruses pose a growing global threat as they are spreading widely, treatment options remain limited, and both climate change and expanding mosquito populations increase the risk of outbreaks worldwide. This review summarizes the determinants of their human tropism, the capacity to infect specific cell types, tissues, and organs. We synthesized current knowledge on how viral factors, including host factor utilization and immune cell trafficking, shape tropism across multiple layers. Central to this process are sequential host barriers that govern infection, including viral attachment, internalization, and replication. Understanding these determinants is essential for informing strategies to mitigate the global burden of these medically important pathogens.

source_records.title: Determinants of orthoflavivirus tropism in humans: from cellular entry to organ-specific pathogenesis
source_records.abstract: Orthoflaviviruses, including dengue virus, tick-borne encephalitis virus, West Nile virus, Zika virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, and yellow fever virus, cause a wide spectrum of diseases in humans despite sharing a similar genomic organization. These viruses pose a growing global threat as they are spreading widely, treatment options remain limited, and both climate change and expanding mosquito populations increase the risk of outbreaks worldwide. This review summarizes the determinants of their human tropism, the capacity to infect specific cell types, tissues, and organs. We synthesized current knowledge on how viral factors, including host factor utilization and immune cell trafficking, shape tropism across multiple layers. Central to this process are sequential host barriers that govern infection, including viral attachment, internalization, and replication. Understanding these determinants is essential for informing strategies to mitigate the global burden of these medically important pathogens.

title: Rapid and convergent evolution of Wolbachia genomes in mosquito cell culture.
abstract: Wolbachia are widespread bacterial symbionts of arthropods that manipulate host reproduction and can confer fitness benefits, such as protection against viral pathogens. Their self-spreading ability coupled with their antiviral effect has been harnessed in health programmes to curb the transmission of dengue virus by Aedes mosquitoes. In this context, a better understanding of evolutionary dynamics over short timescales is critical to inform and improve the efficacy of Wolbachia-based disease control interventions. Moreover, experimental evolution of Wolbachia may provide a powerful approach for generating novel symbiont strains with improved properties for disease control. Here we generated new mosquito cell lines by introducing five Wolbachia strains from Drosophila into the symbiont-free Aedes albopictus Aa23 cell line. Following transinfection, long-read whole-genome sequencing revealed multiple mutations, including structural changes, some of them being associated with major shifts in bacterial density. Signs of convergent evolution, an excess of non-synonymous mutations and comparisons with previous studies, indicate that Wolbachia evolution in cell culture is predominantly driven by selection and occurs faster than in insect hosts. Altogether, our study demonstrates that cell culture is a valuable tool to investigate short-term symbiont evolution, explore the genetic basis of bacterial density regulation and generate higher-density symbiont strains suitable for disease control.

title: Systematic genome analysis enables long-overdue taxonomic reorganization of genus Orthoflavivirus; potential assignment of over 50 new species
abstract: Members of the Orthoflavivirus genus in the family Flaviviridae are primarily vector-transmitted RNA viruses infecting humans, other mammals and birds, including major pathogens such as tick borne encephalitis, West Nile, Zika and dengue viruses. Vector-borne flaviviruses are assigned to the Euflavivirus subgenus of orthoflaviviruses, with more divergent largely unclassified insect-specific flaviviruses, including cell fusing agent virus assigned to the second subgenus, Fusivirus. The currently classified 57 orthoflavivirus species have traditionally been assigned descriptively on the basis of their genome and antigenic relatedness, ecology and host and vector tropisms, although many more orthoflavi-like viruses remain unassigned. To investigate whether species might be demarcated using a fixed genetic divergence threshold, we examined distributions of pairwise distances in NS5 and E genes (which encode the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase and envelope protein, respectively) of classified orthoflaviviruses. Demarcation thresholds of 0.1 in the two regions would be most parsimonious with current euflavivirus classification. Exceptions include species in the tick-borne encephalitis virus complex with divergences below the threshold, and dengue virus types currently assigned to a single species that are substantially above. Application of the proposed thresholds would provide the means to establish 25 new euflavivirus and 33 new fusivirus species and reconcile several anomalies and inconsistencies in the current species taxonomy. The use of a species demarcation threshold brings consistency with the classification of viruses in other families. A robust and evolutionarily consistent framework furthermore enables taxonomic assignments of the numerous currently unassigned orthoflaviviruses that lack the phenotypic descriptions required for the current species definition.

title: Integrating developmental traits, morphometrics and machine learning for sex classification of Aedes aegypti (Diptera: Culicidae).
abstract: Abstract Aedes aegypti (Linnaeus, 1762), the primary vector for dengue, Zika, chikungunya and yellow fever, requires precise sex separation for the effective application of the sterile insect technique. This study integrates developmental biology, morphometric analysis and machine learning to differentiate sexes in Ae. aegypti pupae and adults. We evaluated developmental parameters across six generations of the Old Balara strain. Morphometric data from pupae and adults, including pupal cephalothorax dimensions, pupal length, pupal weight, adult wing length and adult thorax length, were collected to assess their correlations. Pupal morphometrics (cephalothorax dimensions and pupal length and weight) were used to train nine ML models for pupal sex classification. Males pupated significantly earlier (5.61 ± 0.10 days) than females (6.40 ± 0.16 days). In the absence of mating, females lived longer (22.63 ± 0.42 days) than males (20.13 ± 0.34 days). After mating, longevity declined, with females showing a 10.34% reduction (2.34 days) and males a 32.94% reduction (6.63 days). Across all morphometric parameters (cephalothorax length, width and perimeter in mm; cephalothorax area in mm 2 ; pupal length in mm; pupal weight in mg; adult wing length in mm; thorax length in mm), females were significantly larger than males. Pupal cephalothorax perimeter and area strongly correlated with adult thorax and wing lengths ( R 2 up to 0.88), indicating their predictive value for adult size. Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machines and Naïve Bayes achieved 100% accuracy in pupal sex classification on the test set. Integrating morphometric analysis with machine learning significantly enhances sex sorting precision for the sterile insect technique, improving mosquito control efficiency by ensuring only males are released. Future research should explore incorporating image‐based data and advanced machine learning techniques to further refine these methods across diverse mosquito populations.

source_records.abstract: Aedes aegypti (Linnaeus, 1762), the primary vector for dengue, Zika, chikungunya and yellow fever, requires precise sex separation for the effective application of the sterile insect technique. This study integrates developmental biology, morphometric analysis and machine learning to differentiate sexes in Ae. aegypti pupae and adults. We evaluated developmental parameters across six generations of the Old Balara strain. Morphometric data from pupae and adults, including pupal cephalothorax dimensions, pupal length, pupal weight, adult wing length and adult thorax length, were collected to assess their correlations. Future research should explore incorporating image-based data and advanced machine learning techniques to further refine these methods across diverse mosquito populations.
