title: Antiviral Drug Development against RNA Viruses: Progress, Clinical Translation and Persistent Challenges
abstract: Antiviral drug development has produced transformative treatments for some RNA-virus infections while leaving major gaps in acute respiratory, haemorrhagic and enteric disease. The unevenness of progress cannot be explained by target availability alone. This critical narrative review examines how viral biology, pharmacological exposure, disease timing, trial design, resistance and health-system access jointly determine whether an antiviral candidate becomes a clinically useful intervention. Peer-reviewed mechanistic studies, randomised trials, methodological papers and authoritative institutional evidence published from 2000 to 13 August 2026 were critically synthesised, with earlier foundational findings considered where necessary. Durable combination treatment for human immunodeficiency virus and curative direct-acting treatment for hepatitis C show what sustained target validation and clinical development can achieve. Conversely, trials of influenza, coronavirus disease 2019, respiratory syncytial virus, dengue and emerging infections demonstrate the difficulty of translating reductions in viral replication into reliable effects on symptoms, hospitalisation, transmission or survival. Contrasting remdesivir outcomes across disease stages, context-dependent results for oral coronavirus antivirals, a promising but geographically limited paediatric respiratory syncytial virus trial, and dengue human-challenge studies illustrate why positive virological or early clinical findings require precise interpretation. Resistance is shaped by drug mechanism, treatment exposure, viral population dynamics and surveillance quality, rather than by a uniform property of all RNA viruses. Apparent broad-spectrum activity may also reflect assay artefacts or non-physiological experimental systems. Priorities include pharmacologically credible discovery platforms, earlier diagnosis and treatment, adaptive trials with prespecified patient-important endpoints, resistance-informed combinations, outbreak-ready trial infrastructure and affordability planned before licensing. The central conclusion is that antiviral innovation is most effective when molecular specificity, clinically relevant timing and equitable implementation are developed as a connected evidence pathway.
journal: Journal of Advances in Medical and Pharmaceutical Sciences

title: Emerging or Newly Detected? Rethinking Infectious Disease Outbreaks in North Africa
abstract: North Africa sits where climate change, armed conflict and cross-border mobility meet, and each of these moves pathogens. Yet outbreaks in the region are often recognized late, through travel surveillance abroad, single-hospital studies or reference laboratories rather than routine national reporting. This editorial, which opens the special issue on emerging and re-emerging infectious disease outbreaks in North Africa, reviews three microbial fronts: arboviruses such as West Nile, dengue and chikungunya viruses; antimicrobial resistance and conflict-driven cholera; and fungal pathogens, including Candida auris. It summarizes eleven outbreaks reported in the region since 2012 and how each came to light. The gap between reported and actual burden can be large: in eastern Sudan in 2018, surveillance counted 13,978 chikungunya cases, whereas the epidemic was later estimated to have affected about 487,600 people. The editorial argues that many infections called emerging in North Africa are newly detected rather than new, and that the main gap lies in laboratory and surveillance capacity. It calls for integrated One Health surveillance and wider access to molecular and fungal diagnostics.
journal: Sebha University Journal of Medical Sciences

title: Analysis of Cell Populations from Arbovirus-Infected Tissues by Flow Cytometry.
abstract: Arboviruses still represent a major challenge to public health in many parts of the world. Despite shared epidemiological characteristics, each arboviral disorder displays distinct cellular tropism and activation patterns, progressing to immunopathological outcomes that remain not fully elucidated. A deeper understanding of these processes requires methodologies capable of characterizing the often-complex cellular responses. In this context, flow cytometry emerges as a valuable tool, enabling the characterization of heterogeneous cell populations, the assessment of activation and proliferation markers, the quantification of inflammatory mediators, and the detection of cell death pathways. By integrating these parameters, flow cytometry can enhance our understanding of arbovirus pathogenesis, clarify their cellular tropism, and understand immune responses to infection. This methodological article outlines the main steps for applying the technique to different target tissues infected by chikungunya, dengue, yellow fever, and Zika viruses, emphasizing the most effective strategies.

title: Near or Far?
abstract: Dengue fever is a growing public health threat in urban Bangladesh, yet the role of hospital proximity as a spatial determinant of case detection remains largely untested. This chapter examines whether residents living closer to a dengue-treating hospital are more likely to be detected as cases, using cross-sectional survey data from two Dhaka sites: Dhaka Community Medical College Hospital (Boro Moghbazar) and Mugdha Medical College Hospital. Detection declined significantly with distance, and the effect persisted after adjustment for awareness, age, and prior infection, with each additional 100 meters of distance lowering the odds of detection by roughly 5%. Having an affected neighbor was the strongest correlate of detection, indicating fine-scale spatial clustering. Healthcare-worker responses revealed high knowledge but lower preventive practice, suggesting an institutional engagement gap. A divergent pattern in one distant zone coincided with localized drainage construction, suggesting environmental disturbances can temporarily override the proximity effect.
journal: Mitigation Measures for Environmental and Humanitarian Disasters

title: Clinical and etiological profile of children hospitalized with acute undifferentiated febrile illness in South-Eastern Rajasthan, India: a prospective observational study
abstract: Background: Etiological data on acute undifferentiated febrile illness (AUFI) in India come mainly from adults in humid, high-endemicity regions; pediatric data from semi-arid north-west India are sparse. We determined the etiology, laboratory profile, outcomes and laboratory discriminators in hospitalized children in south-eastern Rajasthan. Methods: Prospective observational study at a tertiary teaching hospital in Jhalawar, Rajasthan. Two hundred children aged 2 months–18 years with fever ≤7 days and no identifiable focus after baseline assessment underwent a standardized diagnostic panel. Proportions carry Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Sparse cell counts required Monte Carlo permutation testing (100 000 replicates) with Holm adjustment across 16 comparisons; threshold performance was assessed post hoc. Results: No etiology was identified in 105 children (52.5%, 95% CI 45.6–59.3). Scrub typhus predominated (33, 16.5%, CI 12.0–22.3; 34.7% of resolved diagnoses), then urinary tract infection (25, 12.5%), dengue (22, 11.0%), malaria (10, 5.0%) and enteric fever (5, 2.5%). Enrollment peaked in August–October (88, 44.0%; p<0.001). All laboratory parameters except creatinine differed by diagnosis (adjusted p≤0.002), as did length of stay, complications and defervescence time. Thresholds were specific but insensitive: hemoglobin <80 g/l for scrub typhus (specificity 97.0%, sensitivity 45.5%, likelihood ratio 15.2), platelets <100×109/l for dengue (86.0%, 68.2%, 4.9). Complications affected 39 children (19.5%), intensive care 25 (12.5%); none died. Conclusions: Scrub typhus, not dengue or malaria, led identifiable causes and accounted for most transfusions. Empirical doxycycline warrants evaluation in post-monsoon fever. Routine thresholds modify suspicion but cannot replace specific testing; the unresolved half defines the gap molecular diagnostics must close.

title: CRISPR/Cas12-powered electrochemical biosensor for chikungunya virus DNA detection using gold-modified screen-printed carbon electrodes
abstract: Background and purpose: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) remains a health concern because its symptoms overlap with dengue and Zika, often leading to misdiagnosis. Conventional diagnostic methods, including viral isolation, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), are time-consuming, costly, and dependent on specialized laboratories. This study aimed to develop a rapid, selective, and sensitive electrochemical biosensor integrated with CRISPR/Cas12 for CHIKV DNA detection. Experimental approach: A CHIKV-specific guide RNA targeting a conserved region of the E1 gene was designed in silico and selected by specificity score (99.15) and E-value (1.7). title: An Atlas of Antiviral Therapeutic Outcomes: How Viral Biology Shapes the Reach of Treatment
abstract: Antiviral inhibition does not produce a single therapeutic endpoint: some infections can be cured after finite treatment, others require durable suppression, and others remain difficult to influence because the actionable phase is brief or anatomically inaccessible. These different outcomes reflect the biological state that preserves infection or permits return, the time during which a drug-sensitive process remains causally important, the anatomical space in which consequential virus or viral material resides, and the capacity of viral populations to evolve under therapeutic pressure. Here, we examine these relationships across curable, suppressible, latent, acute, neuroinvasive, and post-acute viral infections. Comparisons among HCV, HIV-1, HBV, HSV, influenza, RSV, dengue, SARS-CoV-2, Ebola virus, CHIKV, and other systems show how persistence architecture, diagnostic timing, tissue pharmacology, host context, and resistance can determine whether antiviral activity translates into virological cure, durable suppression, recurrence control, prevention, or incomplete therapeutic control. Human challenge studies, clinical programs with discordant outcomes, and resistance studies further illustrate where mechanistic activity and therapeutic sufficiency diverge. Across these examples, antiviral outcome depends ultimately on whether treatment can intercept the biological state that determines the subsequent fate of infection.

title: Oropouche Fever Outbreak, Havana, Cuba, June–September 2024
abstract: Oropouche fever emerged nationwide in Cuba in 2024. We investigated the outbreak in Havana; of 549 suspected cases, 189 (34.4%) were confirmed. No cases were severe. Incidence was 8.9/100,000 population and was highest in adults 27–59 years of age (10.2/100,000 population). Three infants tested positive. Dengue cocirculation challenged surveillance.

title: Molecular Diagnosis of Rickettsial Meningoencephalitis With Concurrent Herpes Simplex Virus Type 2 Infection in a Young Female Presenting With Acute Febrile Encephalopathy: A Report on a Rare Case
abstract: Rickettsial CNS infections have been increasingly reported in tropical countries, including India, and are associated with significant morbidity and mortality.Early diagnosis is challenging due to nonspecific presentations, absent rash/eschar, and limited sensitivity of conventional serological tests in the acute phase.Concurrent CNS infection with herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2) is exceedingly rare and further complicates clinical diagnosis and management.This report presents the case of a 28-year-old previously healthy female from Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh, who presented with a 10-day history of intermittent fever, headache, vomiting, decreased appetite, and progressively worsening altered sensorium.Four days before admission, she developed recurrent seizurelike episodes characterized by upward deviation of the eyeballs and jaw clenching.On admission, a neurological examination revealed a Glasgow coma scale (GCS) score of E2V2M5 with neck rigidity suggestive of meningeal irritation.Owing to progressive neurological deterioration and impaired airway protection, she required endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation.Laboratory investigations demonstrated mild neutrophilic leukocytosis, thrombocytopenia, elevated alanine aminotransferase levels, and hypoalbuminemia.A CSF analysis revealed normal glucose and protein concentrations with minimal pleocytosis, while Gram stain and bacterial cultures were negative.Contrastenhanced computed tomography (CECT) and MRI demonstrated only a small calcified occipital granuloma without evidence of acute inflammatory changes.Extensive investigations for common bacterial and tropical infections, including malaria, dengue, enteric fever, scrub typhus, leptospirosis, and bacterial meningitis, were negative.Multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) performed on peripheral blood detected Rickettsia spp.DNA.Subsequent molecular analysis of CSF also demonstrated Rickettsia spp.DNA, confirming CNS involvement, while real-time PCR simultaneously detected HSV-2 DNA, establishing the diagnosis of concurrent Rickettsia spp.meningoencephalitis and HSV-2 encephalitis.The patient initially received empirical intravenous ceftriaxone, vancomycin, and acyclovir.Following molecular confirmation of Rickettsia spp.infection, doxycycline (100 mg twice daily) was initiated while antiviral therapy was continued.The patient demonstrated progressive neurological improvement with recovery of sensorium and a favorable clinical outcome.This case highlights the diagnostic challenges associated with rickettsial CNS infection, particularly in patients lacking classical clinical features and presenting with normal CSF biochemistry and nonspecific neuroimaging findings.Simultaneous molecular detection of Rickettsia spp. in peripheral blood and CSF together with HSV-2 in CSF emphasizes the importance of considering mixed infectious etiologies in patients presenting with acute febrile encephalopathy.Early application of molecular diagnostics enabled prompt institution of targeted therapy and contributed to successful clinical recovery.To the best of our knowledge, this represents one of the very few reported cases of concurrent molecularly confirmed Rickettsia spp.meningoencephalitis and HSV-2 encephalitis worldwide and is likely the first such case reported from India.

investigations demonstrated mild neutrophilic leukocytosis, thrombocytopenia, elevated alanine aminotransferase levels, and hypoalbuminemia.A CSF analysis revealed normal glucose and protein concentrations with minimal pleocytosis, while Gram stain and bacterial cultures were negative.Contrastenhanced computed tomography (CECT) and MRI demonstrated only a small calcified occipital granuloma without evidence of acute inflammatory changes.Extensive investigations for common bacterial and tropical infections, including malaria, dengue, enteric fever, scrub typhus, leptospirosis, and bacterial meningitis, were negative.Multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) performed on peripheral blood detected Rickettsia spp.DNA.Subsequent molecular analysis of CSF also demonstrated Rickettsia spp.DNA, confirming CNS involvement, while real-time PCR simultaneously detected HSV-2 DNA, establishing the diagnosis of concurrent Rickettsia spp.meningoencephalitis and HSV-2 encephalitis.The patient initially received empirical intravenous ceftriaxone, vancomycin, and acyclovir.Following molecular confirmation of Rickettsia spp.infection, doxycycline (100 mg twice daily) was initiated while antiviral therapy was continued.The patient demonstrated progressive neurological improvement with recovery of sensorium and a favorable clinical outcome.This case highlights the diagnostic challenges associated with rickettsial CNS infection, particularly in patients lacking classical clinical features and presenting with normal CSF biochemistry and nonspecific neuroimaging findings.Simultaneous molecular detection of Rickettsia spp. in peripheral blood and CSF together with HSV-2 in CSF emphasizes the importance of considering mixed infectious etiologies in patients presenting with acute febrile encephalopathy.Early application of molecular diagnostics enabled prompt institution of targeted therapy and contributed to successful clinical recovery.To the best of our knowledge, this represents one of the very few reported cases of concurrent molecularly confirmed Rickettsia spp.meningoencephalitis and HSV-2 encephalitis worldwide and is likely the first such case reported from India.

title: Engineering Upd-like to broadly restrict arbovirus infection and vector competence in mosquitoes
abstract: The global expansion of mosquito-borne viruses poses a growing threat to public health, yet the endogenous signals that activate antiviral immunity in mosquito vectors remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify Aedes aegypti Upd as an activator of JAK/STAT signaling that restricts arbovirus infection. Loss of Upd increased infection and dissemination of the flaviviruses ZIKV and DENV, as well as the alphavirus SINV, whereas blood meal inducible midgut overexpression reduced ZIKV and SINV infection. Mechanistically, Upd associated with the extracellular region of the Domeless (Dome) receptor, and Upd deficiency markedly reduced STAT phosphorylation and nuclear accumulation in the midgut. Upd expression was transiently induced in the midgut by an uninfected blood meal but remained elevated following ZIKV challenge, linking physiological responses to blood feeding with antiviral defense. In mammal mosquito transmission models, Upd overexpression reduced viral acquisition from infected hosts, whereas Upd deficiency enhanced viral dissemination and increased transmission following systemic infection. Together, these findings identify Upd as an endogenous regulator of mosquito JAK/STAT signaling and provide proof of principle that temporally targeted Upd expression can reduce arbovirus susceptibility and vector competence.

title: Gut Microbiota Restructuring and Elizabethkingia Enrichment in Aedes albopictus Larvae Under Pyriproxyfen Exposure
abstract: Aedes albopictus transmits dengue, chikungunya, and Zika viruses, and its expanding range, together with widespread insecticide resistance, threatens the sustainability of chemical vector control. Pyriproxyfen (PPF) is an insect growth regulator used in mosquito control, but the relationship between gut bacteria and larval responses to PPF remains poorly characterized. We combined 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing with culture-dependent isolation to characterize gut bacterial communities in Ae. albopictus following acute PPF exposure and identify candidates for functional investigation. The 24 h median lethal concentration (LC50) for the Fuzhou population was 10.27 mg/L. Community profiles were compared among Fuzhou larvae dying at 2× LC50, surviving at 5× LC50, and receiving solvent alone; solvent-treated Foshan laboratory larvae served as an external population reference. Bacterial richness and Shannon diversity were lower in both exposed Fuzhou groups than in the Fuzhou solvent-treated control, and community structure differed among the four groups (PERMANOVA, R2 = 0.797, p = 0.001). Elizabethkingia accounted for 35.0% of bacterial reads in survivors, compared with 22.8% in non-survivors and 7.6% in Fuzhou solvent-treated controls, with significantly higher relative abundance in survivors than in either comparison group. Culture-dependent isolation from survivors yielded 29 isolates representing nine genera, including three isolates assigned to Elizabethkingia anophelis by 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Concordant sequencing and culture-based evidence, together with the recovery of viable isolates, positions Elizabethkingia as a tractable entry point into this question, opening a route to ask whether the larval microbiota can be managed to preserve the efficacy of pyriproxyfen-based control as resistance to other insecticide classes spreads.

title: Obstetric Admissions in the Intensive Care Unit of a Tertiary Care Hospital: Steps for Better Outcome
abstract: Background: Maternal mortality is a crucial issue throughout the world. In Bangladesh, Maternal mortality ratio was 196 (uncertainty range = 159-234) per 100 000 live births. Maternal deaths occurred on the day of delivery is 30% and 6% on one day post-delivery.1 it is necessary to point out those factors for improvement. Objective: This study was focused to identify those factors, attributed to morbidity and mortality among the pregnant women and women in the postpartum period , who needed ICU admission. Methods: This study is a retrospective observational study from January 2024 to December 2025 (two years) in a tertiary care privet hospital, Dhaka. In the study period, 1697 patients got admitted in the two unit of ICU (7+8=15) 15 beds in a same hospital. Total of 57 patients were enrolled in this study. Results: Mean age of patients was 27.87 ± 7.62 years. Most of the patients got admitted in ICU, during postpartum period {42(73.68%)}. Indications for ICU admission were hypoxemic respiratory failure (77.19%), resp distress (57.89%), pulmonary oedema (38.59%), fluid overload (45.61%), & shock (36.84%). Among the study population, 57.89% received NIV, 40.35% got conventional oxygen, 15.78% were on MV, 10.52% on HFNC, 40.35% required vasopressor support, 10.52% needed dialysis & 29.82% needed transfusion. Diagnoses were divided as obstetric and non-obstetric types. Obstetric diagnoses were pregnancy-induced hypertension (n=20, 35.08%), eclampsia (n=15, 26.31%), postpartum hemorrhage (n=16, 28.07%), HELLP syndrome (n=6, 10.52%), peripartum cardiomyopathy (n=4, 7.01%), intra uterine death with MODS (n=2, 3.50%), ruptured ectopic pregnancy (n=7, 12.28%), and abortion (n= 2, 3.50%). Non-obstetric diagnoses were pulmonary oedema (n=15, 26.31%), AKI (n=10, 17.54%), TRALI (n=10, 17.54%), ARDS (n=4, 7.01%), DIC: 5(8.77%), cerebral venus sinus thrombosis: 2(3.50%), MODS:7(12.28%), Sepsis (n=2, 3.50%), Dengue (n=2, 3.50%), PRES (n=5, 8.77%), congenital methemoglobinemia (n=1, 1.75%), TTP (n=1, 1.75%), and acute pancreatitis (n=2, 3.50%). Non-urban patients were younger than urban patients (25.24 ± 5.57 vs 31.62 ± 5.87, p = 0.031) and higher number of primipara pregnancies among non-urban patients than urban group ( 23 vs 2, p = 0.013). Non-urban patients’ length of hospital stays and ICU stay were longer and had more MODS (15.38%) at admission and mortality rate (12.82%) compared to urban population and APACHE II scoring was higher in non-urban (10.35 ± 3.14, vs 6.43 ± 2.59, p = 0.002). Higher severity of metabolic acidosis and lower P/F ratio and higher serum lactate were observed in non-survivor in compared to survivor group. SOFA score was significantly higher in nonsurvivors compared to survivors (6.5 ± 0.83 vs 2.60 ± 1.07; p < 0.0001). The APACHE II score was also significantly higher in non-survivors compared to survivors’ group (15.3 ± 1.09 vs 7.7 ± 0.6; p < 0.0001). The mean hospital stay was significantly longer in nonsurvivors group compared to survivors (9.0 ± 4.9 Vs 5.3 ± 2.4; p < 0.0001). Conclusions: To improve the outcome, attention should be paid to the non-urban early risk assessment, emergency maternal health care and transportation system and increase awareness about obstetric critical care in non-urban area. Bangladesh Crit Care J September 2026; 14 (2): 98-103

title: COINFECTION WITH PLASMODIUM VIVAX AND CHIKUNGUNYA; WHEN FEBRILE ILLNESS EVOLVES INTO HYPERDYNAMIC SHOCK: CASE REPORT
abstract: Coinfection with malaria and chikungunya is a rare presentation and poses a diagnostic challenge., especially since both infections can produce systemic manifestations and hemodynamic compromise. We present the case of a 23-year-old female patient from an urban area with no known past medical history, who presented with a seven-day history of fever, dizziness, generalized weakness, arthralgia, and vomiting. On admission, she was febrile, tachycardic, and hypotensive, with an insufficient hemodynamic response to initial resuscitation with crystalloids, requiring vasopressor support. Advanced cardiovascular evaluation revealed a predominantly vasodilatory and hyperdynamic profile, characterized by high cardiac output, decreased systemic vascular resistance, and preserved stroke volume. Left and right ventricular systolic and diastolic function remained preserved, with adequate TAPSE and MAPSE, and no significant chamber dilation or regional contractility abnormalities. The electrocardiogram and cardiac enzymes showed no evidence of myocardial injury or myocarditis. Studies revealed severe anemia, with a hemoglobin level of 6 g/ dL, and hepatosplenomegaly. Thick blood smear identified Plasmodium. The patient tested positive for vivax, while the PCR test for chikungunya was positive and the dengue test was negative, confirming the coinfection. Intravenous artesunate was initiated, followed by artemether-lumefantrine, in addition to vasoactive support and transfusion of two units of packed red blood cells. The patient experienced progressive hemodynamic recovery and a favorable clinical course. This case highlights the importance of considering vector-borne coinfections and characterizing the hemodynamic phenotype to differentiate vasodilatory shock from cardiogenic compromise.
journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

title: ARBOVIROSES EM POVOS INDÍGENAS: UMA REVISÃO INTEGRATIVA SOBRE EXPOSIÇÃO VIRAL, FATORES AMBIENTAIS E CONHECIMENTOS ECOLÓGICOS TRADICIONAIS
abstract: As arboviroses representam um importante desafio para a saúde pública, especialmente em populações indígenas, cuja exposição aos vírus pode estar relacionada a fatores ambientais, sociais e às interações com diferentes ecossistemas. Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar as evidências científicas sobre a ocorrência de arboviroses em povos indígenas, considerando a exposição viral, os fatores associados à transmissão e a contribuição dos conhecimentos ecológicos tradicionais para a vigilância epidemiológica. Trata-se de uma revisão integrativa da literatura, realizada nas bases de dados BVS, SciELO, Web of Science e PubMed, considerando publicações entre 2016 e 2026. Foram identificados 775 registros e, após a aplicação dos critérios de elegibilidade, quatro estudos foram incluídos na análise. Os resultados evidenciaram a exposição de populações indígenas a diferentes arbovírus, incluindo dengue, Zika, chikungunya e alfavírus associados a ciclos silvestres, além da presença de vetores em ambientes próximos às residências. Também foram identificadas associações entre exposição viral, mobilidade populacional e atividades desenvolvidas em áreas florestais. Adicionalmente, os conhecimentos ecológicos tradicionais demonstraram potencial para contribuir com a compreensão da sazonalidade das doenças transmitidas por vetores. Conclui-se que a vigilância das arboviroses em povos indígenas deve considerar as particularidades ambientais, epidemiológicas e socioculturais de cada território, valorizando a integração entre investigação científica e conhecimentos comunitários. Entretanto, a quantidade reduzida de estudos evidencia a necessidade de ampliar as pesquisas nessa área.

source_records.title: ARBOVIROSES EM POVOS INDÍGENAS: UMA REVISÃO INTEGRATIVA SOBRE EXPOSIÇÃO VIRAL, FATORES AMBIENTAIS E CONHECIMENTOS ECOLÓGICOS TRADICIONAIS
source_records.abstract: As arboviroses representam um importante desafio para a saúde pública, especialmente em populações indígenas, cuja exposição aos vírus pode estar relacionada a fatores ambientais, sociais e às interações com diferentes ecossistemas. Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar as evidências científicas sobre a ocorrência de arboviroses em povos indígenas, considerando a exposição viral, os fatores associados à transmissão e a contribuição dos conhecimentos ecológicos tradicionais para a vigilância epidemiológica. Trata-se de uma revisão integrativa da literatura, realizada nas bases de dados BVS, SciELO, Web of Science e PubMed, considerando publicações entre 2016 e 2026. Foram identificados 775 registros e, após a aplicação dos critérios de elegibilidade, quatro estudos foram incluídos na análise. Os resultados evidenciaram a exposição de populações indígenas a diferentes arbovírus, incluindo dengue, Zika, chikungunya e alfavírus associados a ciclos silvestres, além da presença de vetores em ambientes próximos às residências. Também foram identificadas associações entre exposição viral, mobilidade populacional e atividades desenvolvidas em áreas florestais. Adicionalmente, os conhecimentos ecológicos tradicionais demonstraram potencial para contribuir com a compreensão da sazonalidade das doenças transmitidas por vetores. Conclui-se que a vigilância das arboviroses em povos indígenas deve considerar as particularidades ambientais, epidemiológicas e socioculturais de cada território, valorizando a integração entre investigação científica e conhecimentos comunitários. title: Rich dynamics of a partially degenerate reaction-advection-diffusion mosquito-borne disease model with multiple transmission routes, latent periods and human behavior change
abstract: The spatiotemporal dynamics of mosquito-borne diseases are driven by host movement, vector dispersal, and environmental heterogeneity, while human behavioral responses often considerably modulate intervention effectiveness. To quantitatively capture these factors, we propose a degenerated reaction-advection-diffusion model that unifies multi-route host infections, host-vector transmission, and individual movement, with host psychological factors embedded as an endogenous component of control, yielding a framework more reflective of realistic epidemic settings. A generalized incidence describes direct contact, enhancing model adaptability. By refined estimates and inductive method, we establish the well-posedness of solutions and the existence of a global attractor. Following next-generation operator, the definition of basic reproduction number\, (BRN) $ \mathscr{R}_{0} $ is given, along with its explicit expression. Threshold analysis shows that for $ \mathscr{R}_{0} 1 $, the disease becomes endemic and the model has at least one positive steady state\, (PSS). In particular, in a spatially homogeneous environment without advection, this PSS is globally attractive. Furthermore, with no advection, we derive the GAS of DFSS when $ \mathscr{R}_{0} = 1 $, as well as the asymptotic profiles of PSS as susceptible diffusion rates tend to 0 or infinity. Numerical simulations indicate that a higher advection coefficient greatly reduces the early-stage epidemic size, while human behavior effectively lowers the outbreak peak, especially in high-risk areas during the early phase. Finally, using the Markov chain Monte Carlo\, (MCMC) method, the model successfully fits Zika virus data from Brazil, demonstrating its potential for practical application.

title: Single-cell analysis of West Nile virus infection in brain organoids identified a serine synthesis enzyme as a determinant of viral neural tropism and a druggable antiviral target
abstract: The cellular and molecular determinants of human neuroinvasive West Nile virus (WNV) disease are currently poorly defined. Previous studies of WNV neural infection relied on rodent models and immortalised cell lines that diverge from human brain tissue. Herein, we established a reproducible human cerebral organoid model of WNV infection and profiled it by virus-inclusive single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-Seq) to obtain an understanding of WNV-host interactions in the context of human neural tissue. We found that WNV showed preferential tropism to progenitor cells, immature neurons, and astrocytes, while the mature neurons were largely resistant to infection. Astrocytes were identified as the principal source of interferon (IFN) and the main hub of IFN-signalling, whereas mature neurons expressed little viral RNA-sensing machinery or STAT1 and responded weakly to infection and to IFN. The differential gene expression analysis between WNV-permissive and nonpermissive cells demonstrated that virus-susceptible cells had high baseline expression of the serine synthesis and one-carbon metabolism genes PHGDH, SHMT2, and MTHFD2, which were not induced by infection. RNA-interference and pharmacological inhibition of phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PHGDH) restricted WNV replication, confirming the requirement of this gene for WNV infection. In addition, the FDA-approved drug disulfiram, known to inhibit PHGDH, also reduced viral replication in neural progenitors and cerebral organoids. Overall, these results provide the first comprehensive single-cell-level characterisation of WNV neural infection in human neural tissue. They identify de novo serine synthesis as a metabolic dependency of WNV in human neural cells that can be targeted as a host-directed antiviral therapy.

title: Blood as a readout of human health: A systematic mass spectrometry-based analysis of human plasma proteomes
abstract: Blood proteins are central to clinical research and diagnostics because they can provide information about physiological and pathological processes throughout the body. In particular, the plasma proteome offers a minimally invasive window into systemic biology. Using mass spectrometry-based proteomics, we aim to improve our understanding of the human plasma proteome in both health and disease. However, plasma proteomics remains challenging because protein concentrations span a wide dynamic range, while biological and demographic factors can introduce substantial variation between individuals. We first investigate the plasma proteome in healthy individuals using longitudinal sampling over one year. These analyses show that protein concentrations are generally more variable between individuals than within the same individual over time, although specific proteins, particularly inflammatory markers, can show pronounced temporal changes. We also identify groups of proteins with coordinated changes in a subset of women, suggesting shared biological regulation and highlighting the importance of considering sex-specific and temporal variation when studying the plasma proteome. We then apply longitudinal plasma proteomics to disease settings to investigate dynamic molecular changes during infection and inflammation. In kidney transplant patients experiencing bacterial infections, we observe pronounced acute-phase responses and changes in protein-complex composition, including evidence for altered HDL-associated proteins during inflammation. In a pediatric dengue cohort, we identify proteins associated with disease severity and inflammatory responses, including PTX3 as a potential early marker, and use protein measurements to distinguish severe from mild infection. We further compare plasma and synovial fluid in patients with rheumatoid arthritis to investigate the relationship between systemic and local molecular environments. Many abundant proteins and antibody clones detected in plasma are also present in synovial fluid, whereas proteins reflecting the joint microenvironment are more specifically detected in synovial fluid. These findings suggest that systemic measurements can provide information about molecular processes occurring within affected tissues. Overall, we demonstrate the value of longitudinal plasma proteomics for characterizing biological variation and studying disease-associated molecular changes. We highlight the need for improved analytical sensitivity, reproducible sample handling, and robust statistical approaches, while emphasizing the importance of longitudinal sampling to distinguish biological variation from disease-related changes. Finally, we propose integrating proteomics with genomics and metabolomics, as well as incorporating peptidomics and post-translational modification analysis, to improve biological interpretation and support more meaningful biomarker discovery.

title: Disseny paramètric d un sistema automatitzat d alimentació per a la cria larvària en medi aquàtic aplicat a programes de Tècnica de l Insecte Estèril (TIE)
abstract: [ES] La expansión de enfermedades transmitidas por vectores, como el dengue o la malaria, se ha intensificado en los últimos años como consecuencia de factores como el cambio climático y la creciente movilidad global. Este escenario representa un desafío significativo para la salud pública a nivel mundial, en el que los mosquitos desempeñan un papel determinante como organismos vectores. Ante esta situación, se hace necesario desarrollar soluciones de control que no solo sean eficaces, sino también sostenibles, escalables y compatibles con el entorno. Las estrategias convencionales de control de estos insectos han estado basadas predominantemente en el uso de insecticidas aplicados mediante fumigación. Si bien estos métodos han demostrado cierta efectividad, su aplicación continuada conlleva consecuencias negativas relevantes, como el impacto ambiental, riesgos para la salud humana y la aparición de resistencias. En este contexto, ha surgido como alternativa la Técnica del Insecto Estéril (TIE), un enfoque que consiste en la liberación sistemática de machos estériles que, al aparearse con hembras silvestres, generan huevos inviables y permiten reducir progresivamente la población. A pesar de sus ventajas, la implantación de programas TIE a gran escala presenta importantes limitaciones operativas. En particular, los procesos asociados a la cría masiva de insectos continúan dependiendo en gran medida de tareas manuales, lo que incrementa los costes de producción y dificulta su escalabilidad. Por ello, la automatización de operaciones críticas dentro del ciclo de cría se convierte en un elemento clave para mejorar la eficiencia global del sistema. En este trabajo se presenta el diseño paramétrico de un sistema automatizado de alimentación para la cría larval en medio acuático, orientado a su aplicación en programas TIE. El sistema propuesto aborda una de las tareas más repetitivas y sensibles del proceso, permitiendo un control más preciso del suministro de alimento y reduciendo significativamente la dependencia de intervención humana. El desarrollo del sistema se ha llevado a cabo mediante herramientas de Diseño Asistido por Ordenador (CAD), empleando un enfoque de modelado paramétrico que permite definir relaciones matemáticas y geométricas entre los distintos elementos del diseño. Este planteamiento aporta ventajas clave, como la capacidad de adaptar el sistema a diferentes condiciones de operación y escalas productivas, la rápida modificación del diseño ante cambios en los requisitos, y la posibilidad de optimizar variables críticas del proceso. Asimismo, facilita la generación de configuraciones modulares, su fabricación mediante tecnologías como la impresión 3D y su integración en entornos industriales. source_records.abstract: [ES] La expansión de enfermedades transmitidas por vectores, como el dengue o la malaria, se ha intensificado en los últimos años como consecuencia de factores como el cambio climático y la creciente movilidad global. Este escenario representa un desafío significativo para la salud pública a nivel mundial, en el que los mosquitos desempeñan un papel determinante como organismos vectores. Ante esta situación, se hace necesario desarrollar soluciones de control que no solo sean eficaces, sino también sostenibles, escalables y compatibles con el entorno. Las estrategias convencionales de control de estos insectos han estado basadas predominantemente en el uso de insecticidas aplicados mediante fumigación. Si bien estos métodos han demostrado cierta efectividad, su aplicación continuada conlleva consecuencias negativas relevantes, como el impacto ambiental, riesgos para la salud humana y la aparición de resistencias. En este contexto, ha surgido como alternativa la Técnica del Insecto Estéril (TIE), un enfoque que consiste en la liberación sistemática de machos estériles que, al aparearse con hembras silvestres, generan huevos inviables y permiten reducir progresivamente la población. A pesar de sus ventajas, la implantación de programas TIE a gran escala presenta importantes limitaciones operativas. En particular, los procesos asociados a la cría masiva de insectos continúan dependiendo en gran medida de tareas manuales, lo que incrementa los costes de producción y dificulta su escalabilidad. Por ello, la automatización de operaciones críticas dentro del ciclo de cría se convierte en un elemento clave para mejorar la eficiencia global del sistema. En este trabajo se presenta el diseño paramétrico de un sistema automatizado de alimentación para la cría larval en medio acuático, orientado a su aplicación en programas TIE. El sistema propuesto aborda una de las tareas más repetitivas y sensibles del proceso, permitiendo un control más preciso del suministro de alimento y reduciendo significativamente la dependencia de intervención humana. El desarrollo del sistema se ha llevado a cabo mediante herramientas de Diseño Asistido por Ordenador (CAD), empleando un enfoque de modelado paramétrico que permite definir relaciones matemáticas y geométricas entre los distintos elementos del diseño. Este planteamiento aporta ventajas clave, como la capacidad de adaptar el sistema a diferentes condiciones de operación y escalas productivas, la rápida modificación del diseño ante cambios en los requisitos, y la posibilidad de optimizar variables críticas del proceso. Asimismo, facilita la generación de configuraciones modulares, su fabricación mediante tecnologías como la impresión 3D y su integración en entornos industriales. En conjunto, este trabajo no solo propone una solución técnica concreta, sino que también establece una metodología de diseño flexible y reutilizable, basada en el modelado paramétrico, que puede extenderse a otros procesos dentro de la cría masiva de insectos, contribuyendo así a mejorar la viabilidad y eficiencia de los programas TIE.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study questions the role of antibody-dependent enhancement in severe dengue, as it is widely thought to explain the disease's severity, while acknowledging that other pathobiological steps may also contribute.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a review of existing literature and does not involve a specific study design or population, focusing instead on the broader scientific context of dengue disease and its pathogenesis.
analysis.methods: The methods involve a comprehensive review of published research on dengue virus infection, including references to multiple studies and their findings on antibody-dependent enhancement and other factors contributing to severe dengue.
analysis.main_results: The study highlights that antibody-dependent enhancement is not the sole or primary mechanism responsible for severe dengue, and that multiple interdependent pathobiological steps may play a role in the development of life-threatening disease.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the role of antibody-dependent enhancement in severe dengue is questionable and suggest that other factors may be more significant, offering a novel perspective on the pathogenesis of dengue disease.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform future research on dengue pathogenesis and could influence the development of more effective diagnostic tools, treatments, and vaccines by shifting focus from antibody-dependent enhancement to other contributing mechanisms.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a review of existing literature and does not present original data, which may affect the strength of its conclusions. However, it provides a critical analysis of current understanding and highlights gaps in evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study questions the widely accepted role of antibody-dependent enhancement in severe dengue, suggesting that multiple interdependent pathobiological steps may contribute to the disease's severity. The authors review existing literature to argue that the focus on antibody-dependent enhancement may be misplaced, and that other factors are more significant in the development of life-threatening dengue. The findings may inform future research and influence the development of diagnostic, therapeutic, and preventive strategies for dengue. However, the study is limited to a literature review and does not present original data, which may affect the strength of its conclusions. The evidence is considered moderate due to its reliance on secondary sources and the absence of direct experimental findings.

analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于现有文献的回顾,未提供原始数据,这可能影响其结论的强度。然而,它对当前理解进行了批判性分析,并指出了证据中的空白。

title: A C-terminal fragment of Aedes albopictus salivary protein 34k2 facilitates DENV-2 replication and modulates host inflammation

full_text: Abstract Background Mosquito salivary proteins facilitate arboviral transmission through diverse biological mechanisms, including mechanical transmission, immune regulation. While the Aedes albopictus 34k2 salivary protein enhances DENV-2 infection, its precise functional domain remains unclear. This study aimed to delineate the structural basis of 34k2-mediated DENV-2 enhancement and elucidate its role in viral binding and host immune modulation. Methods Structural prediction (AlphaFold3) and molecular docking (ZDOCK) localized binding interfaces. Two truncated variants were constructed: an N-terminal fragment (rAlb-34k2-I) and a C-terminal fragment (rAlb-34k2-II). Binding affinity was evaluated using surface plasmon resonance (SPR). Viral replication and infectivity were assessed via immunofluorescence, plaque assays, and qRT-PCR in RAW264.7 macrophages and THP-1 monocytes. Immunomodulatory effects of rAlb-34k2-II and rAlb-34k2 were analyzed using qPCR and ELISA in vitro, alongside an in vivo murine footpad injection model. Results Docking identified the viral-binding site within the C-terminal region. SPR confirmed that rAlb-34k2-II bound DENV-2 virions with high affinity (KD = 2.88 nM), whereas rAlb-34k2-I showed no measurable binding. Pre-incubation with rAlb-34k2-II significantly enhanced DENV-2 replication and infectious plaque production in immune cells. Furthermore, both rAlb-34k2-II and the full-length rAlb-34k2 protein significantly upregulated the transcription of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-1β) and chemokines (CCL2, CXCL2) in vitro. This immune response was characterized by a distinct kinetic pattern: a transient early spike in inflammatory cytokines followed by sustained expression of chemokines. Consistent with these in vivo findings, the full-length 34k2 protein induced a similar pro-inflammatory profile in the local murine footpad tissue. Conclusions The C-terminal fragment (residues 148–322) of Ae. albopictus 34k2 constitutes a high-affinity viral-binding domain that potentiates DENV-2 replication and modulates host inflammation. Targeting this specific salivary–viral interface represents a promising rational strategy for developing competitive decoy peptides or next-generation salivary-based vaccines to interrupt arboviral transmission. full_text_sections.full_text: Abstract Background Mosquito salivary proteins facilitate arboviral transmission through diverse biological mechanisms, including mechanical transmission, immune regulation. While the Aedes albopictus 34k2 salivary protein enhances DENV-2 infection, its precise functional domain remains unclear. This study aimed to delineate the structural basis of 34k2-mediated DENV-2 enhancement and elucidate its role in viral binding and host immune modulation. Methods Structural prediction (AlphaFold3) and molecular docking (ZDOCK) localized binding interfaces. Two truncated variants were constructed: an N-terminal fragment (rAlb-34k2-I) and a C-terminal fragment (rAlb-34k2-II). Binding affinity was evaluated using surface plasmon resonance (SPR). Viral replication and infectivity were assessed via immunofluorescence, plaque assays, and qRT-PCR in RAW264.7 macrophages and THP-1 monocytes. Immunomodulatory effects of rAlb-34k2-II and rAlb-34k2 were analyzed using qPCR and ELISA in vitro, alongside an in vivo murine footpad injection model. Results Docking identified the viral-binding site within the C-terminal region. SPR confirmed that rAlb-34k2-II bound DENV-2 virions with high affinity (KD = 2.88 nM), whereas rAlb-34k2-I showed no measurable binding. Pre-incubation with rAlb-34k2-II significantly enhanced DENV-2 replication and infectious plaque production in immune cells. Furthermore, both rAlb-34k2-II and the full-length rAlb-34k2 protein significantly upregulated the transcription of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-1β) and chemokines (CCL2, CXCL2) in vitro. This immune response was characterized by a distinct kinetic pattern: a transient early spike in inflammatory cytokines followed by sustained expression of chemokines. Consistent with these in vivo findings, the full-length 34k2 protein induced a similar pro-inflammatory profile in the local murine footpad tissue. Conclusions The C-terminal fragment (residues 148–322) of Ae. albopictus 34k2 constitutes a high-affinity viral-binding domain that potentiates DENV-2 replication and modulates host inflammation. Targeting this specific salivary–viral interface represents a promising rational strategy for developing competitive decoy peptides or next-generation salivary-based vaccines to interrupt arboviral transmission. full_text: TB preventive treatment benefits people with HIV in the ‘treat all’ era Providing tuberculosis (TB) preventive treatment (TPT) to people living with HIV is associated with fewer TB cases and deaths from all causes, according to a study in The Lancet HIV.1 The study examined its effectiveness in the “treat all” era, when antiretroviral therapy (ART) is recommended for everyone diagnosed with HIV. Researchers analysed electronic health records from more than 235,000 people with HIV in Haiti, Kenya, Nigeria, Uganda, Zimbabwe and Ukraine. The data were collected as part of the Programmatic Effectiveness of Tuberculosis Preventive Treatment for People with HIV in Six High-Tuberculosis-Burden Countries (PROTECT) prospective cohort study. According to the multinational research team, it is the largest real-world evaluation of TPT effectiveness among people with HIV. Across the six countries, starting TPT within eight weeks of entering HIV care was consistently associated with lower TB incidence and mortality. Overall, treatment was associated with a 61% reduction in TB incidence and a 45% reduction in deaths from all causes. Sarita Shah of Emory University and her co-authors say the findings reinforce the importance of TPT as an essential part of HIV care, despite advances in ART. They also highlight the need to sustain its delivery amid global funding pressures. Satellite data reveal pressure on Egypt’s groundwater Agricultural expansion in Wadi El-Assiuti in Egypt’s Eastern Desert over the past two decades is putting unsustainable pressure on groundwater reserves. Groundwater storage declined at an estimated average rate of about 987,000 cubic metres a year between 2003 and 2024, according to a study in Scientific Reports.2 The findings indicate that the aquifer system already operates beyond its sustainable yield, with water being withdrawn faster than it can be replenished. Wadi El-Assiuti is one of the Eastern Desert’s largest drainage basins, although the study focused on its downstream portion. Agricultural land area expanded by about 273% between 2003 and 2024. The expansion reflects the Egyptian government’s efforts to cultivate desert regions to improve food security and accommodate population growth, as outlined in its Egypt 2030 strategy. The study, by Mohammed Hagage of Egypt’s National Authority for Remote Sensing and Space Sciences, combines satellite observations and machine learning to monitor and forecast groundwater changes. Hagage describes it as the first continuous, basin-scale, satellite-derived record of groundwater storage dynamics in Wadi El-Assiuti and similar Eastern Desert aquifer systems. The model projects that groundwater storage will remain severely depleted through to 2030 under current conditions, with no substantial recovery. The analysis used openly available datasets. Hagage says the methods can therefore be applied to other arid aquifer systems where monitoring data are scarce, helping guide groundwater management and sustainable irrigation across water-stressed parts of the Middle East and North Africa. How wildfires shape political participation in Africa People living near large wildfires in Africa are more likely to vote, contact local councillors, attend community meetings and raise issues collectively, according to a study in Nature Communications.3 The findings suggest that these responses are driven mainly by immediate material losses and demands for public services. The researchers found weaker responses in protest participation. The association between wildfire exposure and political participation was stronger among residents of arid regions, people with greater climate literacy or access to information, and members of politically dominant ethnic groups. Researchers from China and Ghana combined Global Fire Atlas records with Afrobarometer surveys of more than 100,000 people in 34 African countries. Their work contributes to a growing body of research on the social and political consequences of climate-related disasters in Africa. It highlights the importance of addressing communities’ immediate needs after disasters to sustain civic engagement and public support for long-term climate adaptation in the Global South. New dinosaur species found in Zimbabwe A new dinosaur species, Musango matusadonaensis, whose remains were found near Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe in 2018, sheds light on the diversity of animals that lived in what is now southern Africa during the Late Triassic, about 210 million years ago. Researchers from the United Kingdom, South Africa and Zimbabwe were involved in the discovery, described in the Journal of Systematic Palaeontology.4 Musango matusadonaensis walked on two legs, measured about 4.5 metres long and weighed an estimated 220 kilograms. According to the research team, led by Paul Barrett of the Natural History Museum in London, the animal was considerably smaller than the giant, long-necked sauropods that evolved later. It is the fifth dinosaur species named from Zimbabwe. Recent discoveries suggest that dinosaur communities varied across southern Africa, challenging earlier assumptions that broadly similar animals lived throughout the region. Study reveals dengue exposure among coastal Kenyan children Relatively little is known about how frequently children in Africa are exposed to dengue virus, one of the world’s most widespread mosquito-borne viral infections. Researchers from the Kenya Medical Research Institute-Wellcome Trust Research Programme examined patterns of exposure over two decades. Their study in Communications Medicine5 found substantial exposure to dengue virus among children growing up in coastal Kenya. The team tested 8,025 blood samples collected annually between 1998 and 2018 from a cohort of 1834 children aged 15 years and younger. Of these samples, 28.5% contained dengue IgG antibodies, indicating previous exposure to the virus. Antibodies were more common in samples from older children. About 2% of samples from children younger than one year contained antibodies, compared with 40% of those from nine to 10 year olds. Antibody prevalence peaked during outbreak years, while the highest rate of new infections was recorded in 2013, coinciding with a large outbreak in coastal Kenya. Dengue often causes no noticeable symptoms. When illness develops, symptoms can range from fever and severe aches to life-threatening bleeding and shock. The researchers call for stronger surveillance to establish how much illness dengue causes among African children and help health services recognise and respond to infections.

full_text: IJBPAS, November, 2026, 15(11): 5227-5233 ISSN: 2277–4998 5227 IJBPAS, November, 2026, 15(11) ENTOMOLOGICAL SURVEILLANCE OF AEDES MOSQUITOES AND DENGUE RISK IN LAKHIMPUR DISTRICT, ASSAM BARUAH S Department of Zoology, North Lakhimpur University, Assam, India *Corresponding Author: Dr. Sangeeta Baruah: E Mail: Sangeeta1chaya@gmail.com https://doi.org/10.31032/IJBPAS/2026/15.11.10578 ABSTRACT An entomological survey was carried out between September 2024 to February 2025 across several urban and semi-urban localities of Lakhimpur district, Assam, to assess the population density of Aedes mosquitoes. The study involved larval sampling techniques commonly used in public health entomology. The data revealed unusually high values for key vector indices: the House Index was recorded at 55.78, the Container Index at 27.22 and the Breteau index at 121.82 during the study period. These figures suggest a significantly heightened risk for a dengue outbreak in the region. As per the breeding preference, discarded tyres were found to be mostly preferred as breeding site (35% positive) as compared to other solid wastes. With the huge population of Aedes and poor fever supervision activities, there is a chance that the people here may have acquired the infection while visiting other high risk cities or some intruder had brought the virus and the high Aedes population have triggered a local transmission. Keywords: Aedes, House Index, Container Index, Breteau Index, Lakhimpur, Assam INTRODUCTION The dengue virus, which is mostly transmitted by infected Aedes mosquitoes, causes dengue fever and its more severe form, dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF). Aedes aegypti, Aedes albopictus, Aedes scutellaris, and Aedes polynesiensis are the main vector species implicated (Wiwanitkit, 2014). Millions of people worldwide are Received 6th Mach 2026; Revised 9th April 2026; Accepted 16th June 2026; Available online 1st Nov. 2026 Baruah S Research Article 5228 IJBPAS, November, 2026, 15(11) afflicted by these diseases, which are among the most common mosquito-borne illnesses today. They also put a great deal of strain on public health systems, particularly in tropical and subtropical areas. In the North Eatern Region, Assam and Arunachal Pradesh showed a significant positive cases of dengue every year [2, 3, 4]. Usually, the dengue positive cases are reported from largest metropolitan areas of the country but past reports indicate that a significant dengue outbreak has occurred in Pasighat, in the East Siang region of Arunachal Pradesh [2, 3]. Furthermore, Itanagar, the state capital of Arunachal Pradesh, has reported a significant number of dengue positive cases [2, 3]. Approximately 70–80% of dengue-positive cases in Assam are reported from the capital city of Kamrup district [4]. Apart from Kamrup district, there were also notable positive dengue cases in Lakhimpur district [5]. There was also a long interstate barrier between the district and Arunachal Pradesh. As a result, people living in border areas are more likely to get the dengue virus, which raises the possibility that the infection may spread throughout the district. 104 positive dengue cases were reported in a sociodemographic and epidemiological investigation conducted between 2012 and 2015 [5]. The actual disease burden is estimated to be much higher, with many cases undiagnosed, unreported and additional cases reported in public/private sectors. Consequent upon the reporting of the positive cases of dengue/DHF from the district each year and several dengue deaths in the state, a rapid entomological survey for Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus was carried out in the Lakhimpur district to find out whether the cases were imported or it was an indigenous transmission. MATERIALS AND METHODS Study Area The study was conducted in Lakhimpur district, located in the northeastern state of Assam. The region features a subtropical monsoon climate with high humidity and significant rainfall, particularly between June and September. These environmental conditions, along with rapid urbanization and insufficient waste management, create ideal breeding sites for Aedes mosquitoes. The study focused on both urban and semi- urban areas of the district, where artificial water containers were commonly found. Baruah S Research Article 5229 IJBPAS, November, 2026, 15(11) Figure 1: Water containing Discarded Household Containers Study Design and Data Collection A cross-sectional survey was conducted over a span of six months, from September 2024 to February 2025. The study combined both field observations and household surveys. Larval surveillance was carried out by inspecting common water- holding containers such as flower pots, discarded tires, plastic buckets, and any kind of water storage containers and tanks in selected neighbourhoods. The survey for Aedes mosquito breeding was carried out in the urban and suburban areas using single larva technique Baruah S Research Article 5230 IJBPAS, November, 2026, 15(11) during September 2024 to February 2025. The larvae were collected, reared till adult emergence and species identification was confirmed using adult dichotomous keys of Darsie and Morris [6]. Each sampled container was emptied completely to destroy the site of breeding. Data Analysis: The density of the larvae of vector mosquitoes was expressed in House Index (HI), Breteau Index (BI) and Container Index (CI). The present study used the following formulae to calculate BI, CI and HI. Container Index (CI): Percentage of wet containers infested with larvae and/or pupae Number of positive containers* CI= ×100 Number of wet container inspected House Index (HI): Percentage of houses infested with larvae and/or pupae Number of houses infested* HI = × 100 Number of houses inspected Breteau Index (BI): Number of positive containers per 100 houses inspected Number of positive containers* BI= × 100 Number of houses inspected *Positive for Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus only RESULTS AND DISCUSSION The entomological survey revealed a high presence of Aedes larvae in various types of man-made containers, particularly during the peak post monsoon months as included in the study. The Breteau Index was found to exceed the threshold level of 20 in several wards, indicating a high risk of dengue transmission. Discarded tires and uncovered water containers were the most common breeding habitats observed. During the study the Aedes were found to prefer discarded tyres mostly as breeding grounds (35%) followed by uncovered water containers and empty flower pots. The preferences for breeding site are shown in Figure 2. Baruah S Research Article 5231 IJBPAS, November, 2026, 15(11) Figure 2: Common Aedes Breeding Sites and Frequency of Larval Detection Between September 2024 and February 2025, larval surveys were conducted in a total of 678 households across different urban and semi-urban areas in Lakhimpur district, Assam. During the course of the survey, 3034 water-holding containers were examined for the presence of Aedes larvae. The data collected showed clear month-to- month variations in the mosquito indices used to assess dengue transmission risk— namely, the House Index (HI), Container Index (CI), and Breteau Index (BI). In September 2024, where every house inspected tested positive for Aedes breeding, leading to a House Index of 100%. The Container Index for that month was 38.08%, and the Berteau Index reached 270.11—well beyond the threshold considered safe by health authorities. High values continued into October and November, with the House Index at 86.46% and 78.20% respectively. The Container Index peaked in October at 58.47%, while the Breteau Index remained elevated in both months (190.63 in October and 166.67 in November), signalling a strong and persistent presence of the mosquito. From December onward, the indices began to decline, likely due to cooler weather and reduced rainfall. In December, the Breteau Index dropped to 107.97. The trend continued into the new year, with January showing a Breteau Index of 66.67, and by February 2025, it had decreased further to 35.13. The House Index also fell sharply to just 11.48 by the end of the survey period, and the Container Index declined to 13.27. A detailed breakdown of the monthly findings is provided in Table 1 and figure 3. The overall pattern suggests a seasonal peak in Aedes mosquito activity during the post-monsoon months, followed by a steady reduction during the winter. These findings emphasize the need for timely mosquito control efforts, especially in the Baruah S Research Article 5232 IJBPAS, November, 2026, 15(11) months leading up to and following the monsoon season. The situation was most alarming in September 2024, where every house inspected tested positive for Aedes breeding. The high entomological indices reflect both environmental and behavioural factors contributing to the proliferation of vectors. Unplanned urban growth and inadequate sanitation infrastructure has been intensifying the issue, creating microhabitats that are difficult to manage through conventional vector control strategies alone. full_text_sections.full_text: IJBPAS, November, 2026, 15(11): 5227-5233 ISSN: 2277–4998 5227 IJBPAS, November, 2026, 15(11) ENTOMOLOGICAL SURVEILLANCE OF AEDES MOSQUITOES AND DENGUE RISK IN LAKHIMPUR DISTRICT, ASSAM BARUAH S Department of Zoology, North Lakhimpur University, Assam, India *Corresponding Author: Dr. Sangeeta Baruah: E Mail: Sangeeta1chaya@gmail.com https://doi.org/10.31032/IJBPAS/2026/15.11.10578 ABSTRACT An entomological survey was carried out between September 2024 to February 2025 across several urban and semi-urban localities of Lakhimpur district, Assam, to assess the population density of Aedes mosquitoes. The study involved larval sampling techniques commonly used in public health entomology. The data revealed unusually high values for key vector indices: the House Index was recorded at 55.78, the Container Index at 27.22 and the Breteau index at 121.82 during the study period. These figures suggest a significantly heightened risk for a dengue outbreak in the region. As per the breeding preference, discarded tyres were found to be mostly preferred as breeding site (35% positive) as compared to other solid wastes. With the huge population of Aedes and poor fever supervision activities, there is a chance that the people here may have acquired the infection while visiting other high risk cities or some intruder had brought the virus and the high Aedes population have triggered a local transmission. Keywords: Aedes, House Index, Container Index, Breteau Index, Lakhimpur, Assam INTRODUCTION The dengue virus, which is mostly transmitted by infected Aedes mosquitoes, causes dengue fever and its more severe form, dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF). Aedes aegypti, Aedes albopictus, Aedes scutellaris, and Aedes polynesiensis are the main vector species implicated (Wiwanitkit, 2014). Millions of people worldwide are Received 6th Mach 2026; Revised 9th April 2026; Accepted 16th June 2026; Available online 1st Nov. 2026 Baruah S Research Article 5228 IJBPAS, November, 2026, 15(11) afflicted by these diseases, which are among the most common mosquito-borne illnesses today. They also put a great deal of strain on public health systems, particularly in tropical and subtropical areas. In the North Eatern Region, Assam and Arunachal Pradesh showed a significant positive cases of dengue every year [2, 3, 4]. Usually, the dengue positive cases are reported from largest metropolitan areas of the country but past reports indicate that a significant dengue outbreak has occurred in Pasighat, in the East Siang region of Arunachal Pradesh [2, 3]. Furthermore, Itanagar, the state capital of Arunachal Pradesh, has reported a significant number of dengue positive cases [2, 3]. Approximately 70–80% of dengue-positive cases in Assam are reported from the capital city of Kamrup district [4]. Apart from Kamrup district, there were also notable positive dengue cases in Lakhimpur district [5]. There was also a long interstate barrier between the district and Arunachal Pradesh. As a result, people living in border areas are more likely to get the dengue virus, which raises the possibility that the infection may spread throughout the district. 104 positive dengue cases were reported in a sociodemographic and epidemiological investigation conducted between 2012 and 2015 [5]. The actual disease burden is estimated to be much higher, with many cases undiagnosed, unreported and additional cases reported in public/private sectors. Consequent upon the reporting of the positive cases of dengue/DHF from the district each year and several dengue deaths in the state, a rapid entomological survey for Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus was carried out in the Lakhimpur district to find out whether the cases were imported or it was an indigenous transmission. MATERIALS AND METHODS Study Area The study was conducted in Lakhimpur district, located in the northeastern state of Assam. The region features a subtropical monsoon climate with high humidity and significant rainfall, particularly between June and September. These environmental conditions, along with rapid urbanization and insufficient waste management, create ideal breeding sites for Aedes mosquitoes. The study focused on both urban and semi- urban areas of the district, where artificial water containers were commonly found. full_text: Le traitement préventif de la tuberculose profite aux personnes vivant avec le VIH à l’ère du « traitement universel » Selon une étude publiée dans The Lancet HIV,1 l’administration d’un traitement préventif contre la tuberculose (TPT) aux personnes vivant avec le VIH est associée à une diminution du nombre de cas de tuberculose et de décès, toutes causes confondues. L’étude a examiné son efficacité à l’ère du « traitement universel », où un traitement antirétroviral (TAR) est recommandé pour toute personne chez qui le VIH a été diagnostiqué. Les chercheurs ont analysé les dossiers médicaux électroniques de plus de 235 000 personnes vivant avec le VIH en Haïti, au Kenya, au Nigeria, en Ouganda, au Zimbabwe et en Ukraine. Les données ont été recueillies dans le cadre de l’étude de cohorte prospective intitulée « Programmatic Effectiveness of Tuberculosis Preventive Treatment for People with HIV in Six High-Tuberculosis-Burden Countries » (PROTECT). Selon l’équipe de recherche multinationale, il s’agit de la plus grande évaluation en conditions réelles de l’efficacité du TPT chez les personnes vivant avec le VIH. Dans les six pays étudiés, le fait de commencer le TPT dans les huit semaines suivant l’entrée en prise en charge du VIH a été systématiquement associé à une incidence et à une mortalité plus faibles liées à la tuberculose. Globalement, le traitement a été associé à une réduction de 61% de l’incidence de la tuberculose et à une réduction de 45% des décès toutes causes confondues. Sarita Shah, de l’université Emory, et ses coauteurs affirment que ces résultats soulignent l’importance du TPT en tant qu’élément essentiel de la prise en charge du VIH, malgré les progrès réalisés en matière de traitement antirétroviral (TAR). Ils mettent également en évidence la nécessité de maintenir sa mise en œuvre malgré les pressions financières mondiales. Des données satellitaires révèlent une pression sur les nappes phréatiques en Égypte L’expansion agricole dans le Wadi El-Assiuti, dans le désert oriental égyptien, au cours des deux dernières décennies, exerce une pression insoutenable sur les réserves d’eau souterraines. Selon une étude publiée dans Scientific Reports2 , les réserves d’eau souterraines ont diminué à un rythme moyen estimé à environ 987 000 mètres cubes par an entre 2003 et 2024. Ces résultats indiquent que le système aquifère fonctionne déjà au-delà de son rendement durable, l’eau étant prélevée plus rapidement qu’elle ne peut être renouvelée. Le Wadi El-Assiuti est l’un des plus grands bassins versants du désert oriental, bien que l’étude se soit concentrée sur sa partie aval. La superficie des terres agricoles a augmenté d’environ 273% entre 2003 et 2024. Cette expansion reflète les efforts du gouvernement égyptien visant à cultiver les régions désertiques afin d’améliorer la sécurité alimentaire et de répondre à la croissance démographique, comme le prévoit sa stratégie « Égypte 2030 ». Cette étude, menée par Mohammed Hagage de l’Autorité nationale égyptienne pour la télédétection et les sciences spatiales, combine des observations satellitaires et l’apprentissage automatique pour surveiller et prévoir l’évolution des eaux souterraines. M. Hagage la décrit comme le premier enregistrement continu, à l’échelle du bassin et issu de données satellitaires, de la dynamique des réserves d’eau souterraines dans le Wadi El-Assiuti et dans des systèmes aquifères similaires du désert oriental. Le modèle prévoit que les réserves d’eau souterraines resteront gravement épuisées jusqu’en 2030 dans les conditions actuelles, sans reprise significative. L’analyse a utilisé des ensembles de données librement accessibles. M. Hagage précise que ces méthodes peuvent donc être appliquées à d’autres systèmes aquifères arides où les données de surveillance sont rares, contribuant ainsi à orienter la gestion des eaux souterraines et l’irrigation durable dans les régions du Moyen-Orient et d’Afrique du Nord confrontées à un stress hydrique. Comment les feux de forêt influencent la participation politique en Afrique Les personnes vivant à proximité de grands feux de forêt en Afrique sont plus enclines à voter, à contacter les élus locaux, à assister à des réunions communautaires et à soulever des problèmes de manière collective, selon une étude publiée dans Nature Communications.3 Les résultats suggèrent que ces réactions sont principalement motivées par les pertes matérielles immédiates et les demandes de services publics. Les chercheurs ont constaté que la participation aux manifestations était moins marquée. Le lien entre l’exposition aux feux de forêt et la participation politique était plus marqué chez les habitants des régions arides, les personnes disposant d’une meilleure connaissance du climat ou d’un meilleur accès à l’information, ainsi que chez les membres des groupes ethniques politiquement dominants. Des chercheurs chinois et ghanéens ont combiné les données du Global Fire Atlas avec les enquêtes Afrobaromètre menées auprès de plus de 100 000 personnes dans 34 pays africains. Leurs travaux s’inscrivent dans un corpus croissant de recherches sur les conséquences sociales et politiques des catastrophes liées au climat en Afrique. Il souligne l’importance de répondre aux besoins immédiats des communautés après une catastrophe afin de maintenir l’engagement civique et le soutien du public en faveur d’une adaptation climatique à long terme dans les pays du Sud. Une nouvelle espèce de dinosaure découverte au Zimbabwe Une nouvelle espèce de dinosaure, Musango matusadonaensis, dont les restes ont été découverts près du lac Kariba au Zimbabwe en 2018, apporte un éclairage sur la diversité des animaux qui vivaient dans ce qui est aujourd’hui l’Afrique australe au Trias supérieur, il y a environ 210 millions d’années. Des chercheurs du Royaume-Uni, d’Afrique du Sud et du Zimbabwe ont participé à cette découverte, décrite dans le Journal of Systematic Palaeontology.4 Musango matusadonaensis marchait sur deux pattes, mesurait environ 4,5 mètres de long et pesait, selon les estimations, 220 kilogrammes. Selon l’équipe de recherche, dirigée par Paul Barrett du Musée d’histoire naturelle de Londres, cet animal était nettement plus petit que les sauropodes géants à long cou qui ont évolué par la suite. Il s’agit de la cinquième espèce de dinosaure répertoriée au Zimbabwe. Des découvertes récentes suggèrent que les communautés de dinosaures variaient à travers l’Afrique australe, remettant en cause les hypothèses antérieures selon lesquelles des animaux globalement similaires vivaient dans toute la région. Une étude révèle l’exposition à la dengue chez les enfants des zones côtières du Kenya On sait relativement peu de choses sur la fréquence à laquelle les enfants africains sont exposés au virus de la dengue, l’une des infections virales transmises par les moustiques les plus répandues au monde. Des chercheurs du Programme de recherche du Kenya Medical Research Institute-Wellcome Trust ont examiné les schémas d’exposition sur deux décennies. Leur étude, publiée dans Communications Medicine,5 a mis en évidence une exposition importante au virus de la dengue chez les enfants vivant sur la côte kenyane. L’équipe a analysé 8 025 échantillons sanguins prélevés chaque année entre 1998 et 2018 auprès d’une cohorte de 1 834 enfants âgés de 15 ans et moins. Parmi ces échantillons, 28,5% contenaient des anticorps IgG anti-dengue, indiquant une exposition antérieure au virus. Les anticorps étaient plus fréquents dans les échantillons provenant d’enfants plus âgés. Environ 2% des échantillons prélevés chez des enfants de moins d’un an contenaient des anticorps, contre 40% chez ceux âgés de 9 à 10 ans. La prévalence des anticorps a atteint son pic pendant les années d’épidémie, tandis que le taux le plus élevé de nouvelles infections a été enregistré en 2013, coïncidant avec une importante épidémie sur la côte kenyane. La dengue ne provoque souvent aucun symptôme perceptible. Lorsque la maladie se déclare, les symptômes peuvent aller de la fièvre et de douleurs intenses à des hémorragies et un choc pouvant mettre la vie en danger. Les chercheurs appellent à un renforcement de la surveillance afin de déterminer l’ampleur de la charge de morbidité liée à la dengue chez les enfants africains et d’aider les services de santé à reconnaître les infections et à y répondre.
